title: Decomposing Irregular Time Series into Interpretable Temporal Patterns with Mixture-of-Experts
summary: Irregularly-spaced sequential data, such as transaction logs, encode multi-scale temporal structure that is critical for prediction but difficult to recover explicitly with standard sequence models, which often trade interpretability for performance. We introduce MoTIF, an interpretable framework using mixture-of-experts (MoE) attention to decompose irregular time series into temporal patterns spanning minute-to-year scales. Each expert is trained via temporal alignment that induces attention specialization to a designated cyclical or within-range pattern, with label-free routing supervision that learns to activate the correct expert from patterns present in the data. On synthetic data with known temporal structure, MoTIF recovers correct routing well above chance (0.389/0.829 for range/cyclical patterns vs. 0.091 random) and outperforms all baselines, including a standard transformer and an unspecialized MoE, on next-value prediction. On a public credit card transaction dataset, MoTIF achieves higher macro-F1 than all baselines for next-amount prediction. Its learned routing reveals structure a black-box model cannot: transactions are governed primarily by intraday and short-interval rhythms, while fraudulent transactions show bursty, calendar-agnostic timing versus the steadier periodicity of legitimate ones. On downstream fraud detection, MoTIF matches standard transformer and MoE baselines and clearly outperforms recent sequential recommendation models used as embedding baselines. These results show that decomposing temporal structure into interpretable, expert-specific patterns need not sacrifice predictive accuracy, offering a practical route to sequence models that are both accurate and auditable in high-stakes settings. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MoTIF-82E4.
core_methodology: MoTIF uses mixture-of-experts (MoE) attention to decompose irregular time series into interpretable temporal patterns across multiple time scales. The method employs specialized experts for cyclical and range-based patterns with label-free routing supervision for improved interpretability and prediction accuracy.
data_sources: Public credit card transaction dataset, synthetic data with known temporal structure
alpha_potential: The method can extract multi-scale temporal patterns from irregularly-spaced financial data (e.g., transaction logs, tick data), potentially identifying profitable market rhythms (in intraday trading, high-frequency trading) or detecting anomalous patterns (fraud detection, market manipulation patterns). The interpretability advantage could be valuable for auditability in regulated trading contexts.
title_cn: 使用专家混合模型将不规则时间序列分解为可解释的时间模式
summary_cn: 本研究提出的MoTIF框架通过专家混合注意力机制分解不规则时间序列(如交易日志),可发现分钟到年级别的市场节奏。在信用卡交易数据上能显著提升预测精度,其可解释的路由机制可区分正常交易的周期性模式与欺诈交易的突发性特征。该方法可直接应用于高频交易节奏分析、异常交易检测等量化场景,在保持预测精度的同时满足金融审计需求。

title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions. AStockArena reconstructsthe actions actually posted to accounts by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states, and audits them with eight checks spanning execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B), combining record verification with consensus expert annotation. Of 1,070 trading points, 72.99% exhibit at least one audit gap; model-level rates range from52.2% to 91.2%, with evidence gaps most prevalent. Historical trade-filtering replay further shows thatportfolio outcomes are sensitive to these flagged trades. Decision-process auditing thus offers a verifiable complement to return-based evaluation of financial agents.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for financial trading agents, focusing on execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B) through eight checks. It reconstructs actions by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states.
data_sources: China's A-share market data, including real-time trading reports, execution responses, and account states.
alpha_potential: The auditing framework identifies and flags trades with execution gaps, which historically impact portfolio outcomes. This suggests potential alpha in improving trade execution quality and reliability of financial agents.
title_cn: AStockArena：超越回报，我们能将真实资本托付给金融代理的决策吗？
summary_cn: 本文提出了AStockArena，一个针对中国A股市场的实时决策审计基准，通过八个审计检查评估金融代理的执行可追溯性、证据充分性和财务元意识。研究发现72.99%的交易点存在至少一个审计缺口，影响投资组合结果，为量化交易提供了质量控制的创新方法。

title: MarkovTS: Pretrained State-Transition Representations for Zero-Shot Time Series Generation
summary: Across heterogeneous real-world domains, time-series generation supports simulation, model development, and data augmentation by generating sequences that preserve target-domain statistics and temporal dependencies when real observations are scarce or costly. However, existing methods predominantly address in-domain generation, limiting their reuse in unseen domains. We study reference-conditioned zero-shot time series generation: target domains are unseen during pretraining, generation uses a single target-domain reference sequence, and no model parameters are updated. MarkovTS characterizes sequence evolution through local morphologies and their ordered transitions at multiple temporal scales. Its pretrained encoder quantizes normalized time-series patches into multiscale morphological states with a state codebook, while a transition codebook encodes contextual transitions between adjacent intervals. These transferable state-transition representations condition a pretrained flow-matching model. At generation, the frozen model combines a reference-derived condition with independent Gaussian noise to produce stochastic samples that retain the reference's temporal organization. Across 12 unseen target datasets, MarkovTS outperforms strong baselines in most distributional comparisons and generates diverse, reference-consistent sequences. As downstream augmentation, its samples yield overall gains across forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection benchmarks and diverse model families. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/MarkovTS.
core_methodology: MarkovTS uses a pretrained encoder to quantize time-series patches into multiscale morphological states and encodes transitions between these states. These representations condition a flow-matching model for zero-shot generation of time-series data that preserves the reference sequence's temporal dependencies.
data_sources: Generic time-series data for pretraining; requires a single target-domain reference sequence for zero-shot generation. In finance, could use market data (OHLC, volumes, etc.) as reference.
alpha_potential: High potential for generating synthetic market data that preserves key statistical properties. Can augment scarce historical data (e.g., during rare market regimes) for improved backtesting and model training. May help simulate market conditions for robust strategy development.
title_cn: MarkovTS：用于零样本时间序列生成的预训练状态转移表示
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种零样本时间序列生成方法，通过多尺度状态转移表示可生成与参考序列具有相同统计特性和时间依赖性的合成数据。在量化交易中，可用于市场数据增强、罕见市场环境模拟，以及提高模型在数据稀缺情况下的鲁棒性，具有直接的策略开发和回测应用价值。

title: Best-of-Both-Worlds FTRL for Linear Bandits: The Interplay of Information Acquisition, Corruption, and Geometry
summary: We study \textit{best-of-both-worlds} (BOBW) algorithms for linear bandits, which aim to simultaneously guarantee $\gO(\sqrt T)$ regret in the adversarial regime and $\gO(\log T)$ regret in the stochastic regime over $T$ rounds. For finite action sets, we introduce \emph{information-acquisition follow-the-regularized-leader} (\IAFTRL{}), the first BOBW algorithm based purely on the follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) framework that attains an $\gO(\cstar\log T)$-type regret in the stochastic regime, where $\cstar$ is the information-acquisition complexity that characterizes instance-dependent optimality in linear bandits, while retaining the $\gO(\sqrt{T})$ regret guarantee in the adversarial regime. This resolves the open problem posed in~\cite{LeeEtAl2021,KongZ023,ItoT23,ZhaoItoLi2025}.
core_methodology: Follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) framework adapted for linear bandits with information-acquisition complexity consideration, providing best-of-both-worlds guarantees (logarithmic regret in stochastic regimes and square-root regret in adversarial regimes)
data_sources: Generic linear bandit setting applicable to financial data streams where actions correspond to asset selections or portfolio weights
alpha_potential: Provides theoretical foundation for adaptive strategies that can handle both mean-reverting and trending market conditions without prior regime knowledge, particularly valuable for algorithmic trading in changing volatility regimes
title_cn: 线性老虎机的最佳两界FTRL算法：信息获取、干扰与几何结构的相互作用
summary_cn: 该研究提出的IAFTRL算法通过信息获取复杂度优化，在随机机制下实现O(logT)遗憾值，同时保持对抗机制下的O(√T)保证。此自适应方法为量化交易提供了处理不同市场状态（均值回归/趋势跟踪）的理论框架，特别适合需要动态调整策略参数的算法交易系统。

title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
summary: The limit order book (LOB) records outstanding buy and sell orders across multiple price levels. Its state evolves over time across market side, price level, and order attribute, naturally forming a multiway structure. However, existing LOB models typically flatten these dimensions into a matrix model, thus obscuring the existing structural relationships. Starting from first principles and the market-microstructure intuition of the LOB, we design TensorLOB to operate entirely in the tensor domain. TensorLOB uses mode-wise tensor contractions for feature extraction and directly contracts the learned representation with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, retaining the distinct roles of time, side, level, and attribute modes. Experiments on the FI-2010 benchmark show that TensorLOB achieves the highest accuracy, recall, and F1 score across all four evaluated horizons. This proof of concept highlights the potential of high-dimensional modelling of multi-way latent information intrinsic to financial markets, which has so far been largely overlooked.
core_methodology: Tensor-based learning for multiway structure preservation in limit order book data, using mode-wise tensor contractions for feature extraction and low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction.
data_sources: Limit order book (LOB) data across multiple price levels, market sides, and order attributes, specifically evaluated on the FI-2010 benchmark.
alpha_potential: The method captures latent high-dimensional relationships in LOB data that traditional matrix-based models miss, potentially uncovering more precise predictive signals for short-term price movements and market microstructure anomalies.
title_cn: TensorLOB：用于限价订单簿预测的结构保持张量学习
summary_cn: TensorLOB 通过张量运算直接建模限价订单簿的多维度结构（时间、买卖方向、价格档位、订单属性），避免了传统矩阵降维导致的结构信息损失。在 FI-2010 基准测试中实现最高预测精度，证明张量方法能有效捕捉市场微观结构中隐含的高维信号，对高频交易和订单流分析具有实用价值。

title: Can We Stop the Backtest Yet? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Adaptive Financial Research Agents
summary: Financial research agents can generate and monitor trading rules faster than a human can document the resulting selection process. Candidates appear at data-dependent times, weak rules are abandoned, and promising ones are watched until they cross a reporting threshold. We introduce PROMOTE, a protocol that assigns every candidate predictable testing wealth at birth and accumulates a cost-aware e-process only from subsequent returns. If lifetime allocations sum to at most one, a weighted Ville argument bounds the probability of ever promoting a rule whose declared bounded net score has always had nonpositive conditional mean. The result permits dependent candidates, adaptive births, and indefinite monitoring. We audit the implementation in two settings. A retrospective pseudo-out-of-sample replay contains 24 panel--rule hypotheses, 3,000 shared-sign null paths, injected alternatives, and public ETF and industry data. Repeated unadjusted tests produce a family crossing in 94.5% of null paths, versus 0.0% for PROMOTE; at a 15-bp aligned ETF-component perturbation, PROMOTE has 70.1% target power and median crossing session 2,327. A separate exact mean-zero experiment lets an agent select candidate identities and birth times from past scores; the funded gate has 1.77% false-family crossings across 3,000 programs. The market replay produces zero promotions after costs. The certificate controls historical false promotion under the declared null; it is not a certificate that an earlier edge remains profitable at deployment. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces PROMOTE, a protocol for anytime-valid testing of trading rules, which uses e-processes to control false discovery rates in adaptive research environments. It allows for dependent candidates, adaptive births, and indefinite monitoring while maintaining statistical validity.
data_sources: The implementation is audited using pseudo-out-of-sample replay with panel-rule hypotheses and shared-sign null paths, including public ETF and industry data. A separate exact mean-zero experiment is also conducted.
alpha_potential: PROMOTE provides a robust framework for identifying trading rules with non-zero mean returns while controlling false positives. Its adaptive nature allows for dynamic rule selection and monitoring, which could lead to more efficient discovery of alpha-generating strategies.
title_cn: 我们可以停止回测了吗？自适应金融研究代理的随时有效推广测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出了PROMOTE协议，用于在自适应金融研究环境中控制交易规则的假发现率。通过使用e-processes，该方法允许动态规则选择和无限期监控，同时保持统计有效性。在ETF和行业数据的实验中，PROMOTE显著降低了假阳性率，同时保持了较高的目标检测能力。

title: Penalize the Common Trade: A Collision-Aware Layer for Learned Portfolios
summary: Different learning systems can make nearly the same trade when they share data, objectives, or representations. The market then sees decision concentration even if the models look diverse. We call exposure to this shared direction a signal collision. A linear-impact game shows the basic externality: each allocator chooses too much common exposure because it does not bear the full price effect imposed on others. An overlap-dependent toll recovers the social choice, and a feedback model gives the exact gain at which return-responsive allocation becomes unstable. We also state the restrictive spectral conditions under which a leading eigenportfolio can reveal the collision direction. These results motivate a simple post-model layer: subtract a penalty for loading on the recent common return mode before forming the portfolio. In a frozen panel of ten liquid cross-asset ETFs, 760 completed weeks from January 2012 through July 2026, and exact self-financing costs of 10 basis points per dollar traded, this layer changes maximum drawdown from 23.6% to 14.1%, volatility from 12.6% to 10.7%, and excess-return Sharpe from 0.664 to 0.667. A volatility-matched momentum diagnostic still draws down 19.9%. Paired stationary-bootstrap uncertainty is wide: the 95% interval for drawdown improvement is $[-3.3,18.4]$ percentage points and includes zero. The result establishes a reproducible risk-control association and specifies the holdings-and-flow validation needed to attribute the common direction to AI crowding. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a collision-aware layer for learned portfolios that penalizes common trades across different learning systems. It uses a linear-impact game to model the externality of shared exposures and proposes a penalty for loading on recent common return modes to improve portfolio performance.
data_sources: The study uses a frozen panel of ten liquid cross-asset ETFs, covering 760 weeks from January 2012 through July 2026, with exact self-financing costs of 10 basis points per dollar traded.
alpha_potential: The methodology addresses the inefficiency caused by signal collisions and shared exposures in algorithmic trading, leading to improved risk-adjusted returns (Sharpe ratio increase from 0.664 to 0.667) and reduced drawdown (23.6% to 14.1%).
title_cn: 惩罚共同交易：一种用于学习投资组合的碰撞感知层
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种碰撞感知层，通过惩罚学习系统间的共同交易来减少信号碰撞，从而优化投资组合表现。在2012年至2026年十种流动性跨资产ETF的数据测试中，该方法显著降低了最大回撤（23.6%至14.1%）并提高了风险调整后收益（夏普比率从0.664提升至0.667）。

title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: This study aims to determine whether the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) as a specialized execution overlay can enhance pair trading in highly volatile cryptocurrency markets. Although classical implementations of the strategy have proven successful in traditional equities, they frequently exhibit rigidity and suffer from severe divergence risks when applied to high-variance environments. To construct a robust system, we developed a hierarchical "Filter-then-Rank" pair selection methodology and a custom "Fixed Risk, Adaptive Mean" execution model. The system employs a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layer to govern execution decisions within strict deterministic risk management boundaries. Evaluated on 1-hour interval data from the Binance USD-M Futures market, the selected RL policy achieved an Out-Of-Sample performance that substantially outperformed the heuristic baseline, although the results varied considerably across five random seeds, with four of the five seeds exceeding the baseline in both CAGR and Sortino Ratio. A stationary circular block bootstrap test of the Agent's risk-adjusted outperformance yields p-values of approximately 0.06, which fall just short of the conventional 5% significance threshold. Ultimately, this study contributes to the quantitative finance literature by introducing a hybrid architecture that combines statistical arbitrage with DRL execution policies. Furthermore, it applies safe reinforcement learning via deterministic shielding, with results indicating that anchoring a neural policy to statistically robust boundaries mitigates severe divergence risks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a hybrid 'Filter-then-Rank' pair selection methodology and a 'Fixed Risk, Adaptive Mean' execution model using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LSTM for dynamic execution in pair trading. It combines statistical arbitrage with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and employs deterministic shielding for risk management.
data_sources: 1-hour interval data from the Binance USD-M Futures market.
alpha_potential: The strategy leverages the volatility of cryptocurrency markets to enhance pair trading performance through adaptive execution, mitigating severe divergence risks common in high-variance environments. The hybrid approach shows potential for consistent outperformance in statistical arbitrage.
title_cn: 基于深度强化学习的加密货币市场动态多对交易策略
summary_cn: 本研究通过深度强化学习（DRL）增强高波动性加密货币市场的配对交易策略。采用'筛选后排序'的配对选择方法和'固定风险，自适应均值'执行模型，结合PPO和LSTM进行动态决策。在Binance USD-M期货市场的1小时数据上测试，结果显示该方法在风险调整后表现优于基准，且通过确定性屏蔽技术有效控制了发散风险。

title: HARN: Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network for Event-Driven Multi-Timeframe Forecasting
summary: Live financial forecasting must synchronize asynchronous bar completions across timeframes without using stale or unavailable information. We introduce HARN (Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network), an event-driven architecture that anchors each event to the finest configured timeframe and maintains persistent states and matrix-valued associative memories across temporal levels. Its timestamp-masked transition updates a level only when its completed-bar timestamp matches the current anchor, preserving inactive representations. HARN integrates causal multi-scale encoding, residual-driven gated associative writes, all-to-all cross-level resonance, and ordered bottom-up evidence aggregation to produce forecasts at each temporal level. Predictions are expressed as basis-point changes and reconstructed on the price scale for evaluation. We evaluate HARN on four assets spanning equities, foreign exchange, and gold (AAPL, EURUSD, USDCHF, and XAUUSD), using chronological 70/15/15 splits, 32-bar lookbacks, one-step horizons, and three random seeds. HARN obtains lower anchor-timeframe test mean absolute errors (MAEs) than the evaluated single-timeframe PatchTST and TimeXer baselines on all four assets. HARN's MAEs are 0.508, 0.000306, 0.000263, and 2.552, respectively; PatchTST records 2.074, 0.000759, 0.000638, and 9.563, while TimeXer records 2.882, 0.010838, 0.014144, and 15.297. These descriptive comparisons do not isolate architectural effects from differences in inputs, target formulations, or training procedures. Single-run component ablations on AAPL and EURUSD show small, non-monotonic differences. The results demonstrate HARN's feasibility for asynchronous multi-timeframe forecasting, while motivating controlled comparisons and broader ablations to establish its relative advantages and component contributions.
core_methodology: HARN (Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network) is an event-driven architecture for multi-timeframe forecasting that uses timestamp-masked transitions, causal multi-scale encoding, residual-driven gated associative writes, and all-to-all cross-level resonance to maintain persistent states and matrix-valued associative memories across temporal levels.
data_sources: The paper evaluates HARN on four assets: AAPL (equities), EURUSD (foreign exchange), USDCHF (foreign exchange), and XAUUSD (gold). The data is split chronologically into 70/15/15 for training, validation, and testing, with 32-bar lookbacks and one-step horizons.
alpha_potential: HARN demonstrates superior performance in multi-timeframe forecasting compared to single-timeframe baselines (PatchTST and TimeXer), suggesting potential alpha generation through more accurate and synchronized predictions across different timeframes. This could be valuable for high-frequency trading, algorithmic execution, and multi-timeframe strategy development.
title_cn: HARN：用于事件驱动多时间框架预测的层次关联共振网络
summary_cn: HARN是一种事件驱动的多时间框架预测架构，通过层次关联共振网络和异步时间框架同步技术，显著提高了金融时间序列预测的准确性。在AAPL、EURUSD等四种资产上表现优于单时间框架基线模型，适用于高频交易和多时间框架策略开发。

title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs). These algorithms primarily target forward MDPs whose dynamics evolve over time from an initial state. However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics. As a consequence, they cannot be expressed as a standard MDP, thereby calling for a novel theory for RL in this context. Accordingly, this work introduces the concept of Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems, develops a novel theoretical framework to characterize their optimal solutions, and proposes a general forward-backward step-wise template that allows to adapt RL algorithms for FB-MDP problems. A Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) algorithm is introduced accordingly to obtain optimal policies with guaranteed convergence and a competitive rate with respect to standard approaches in RL. FB-MOAC is evaluated on diverse use cases in the context of mathematical finance and mobile resource management. The obtained results show that FB-MOAC outperforms the state of the art across different metrics, highlighting its ability to learn and maximize rewards.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems and develops a novel RL algorithm called FB-MOAC (Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic) that handles both forward and backward dynamics in decision processes. The algorithm guarantees convergence and competitive performance compared to standard RL approaches.
data_sources: The paper evaluates FB-MOAC on diverse use cases, including mathematical finance, though specific market data types (e.g., price series, order book data) are not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: FB-MOAC's ability to handle multi-objective problems with forward-backward dynamics could be valuable for portfolio optimization, dynamic hedging, or execution strategies where decisions depend on both past and future states. The convergence guarantees and competitive performance suggest potential for robust trading strategies.
title_cn: FB-MOAC：一种用于前后向马尔可夫决策过程的强化学习算法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新型强化学习算法FB-MOAC，专门针对具有前后向动态的多目标决策问题。在金融数学的应用测试中表现优异，可潜在应用于投资组合动态优化、算法交易等需要同时考虑历史与未来状态的量化交易场景。

title: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents
summary: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. A common approach is compaction, where the model replaces its history with a self-generated note. Yet off-the-shelf agentic models, including GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.3, often write ineffective notes, and reinforcement learning (RL) alone rarely discovers useful note-taking behavior. We present MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B and trained to manage its context through compaction. We first bootstrap note-taking by fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, then reinforce it with RL using a reward that combines answer correctness, note-quality heuristics, and confidence calibration. Although trained only to compact into a fresh window, MEMENTO extends at test time to strategies such as context folding and confidence-based backtracking. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, with books of up to 2.5M tokens, MEMENTO raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context. It outperforms GPT-5.5 agent in the same harness (13.1%) and full book context (56.7%) at less than 1/50 the cost. It also nearly matches a ~100x larger GLM-5.3 agent (69.3%) at 1/9 the cost, and comes within 6.4 points of GLM-5.3 full context at 1/26 the cost.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MEMENTO, a method for long-context processing in LLM agents using a combination of fine-tuning with synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, reinforced with RL using a composite reward function. The methodology includes context compaction, context folding, and confidence-based backtracking to manage long inputs efficiently.
data_sources: Synthetic trajectories and book-level question answering benchmarks (books up to 2.5M tokens).
alpha_potential: The method's ability to efficiently manage and process long-context inputs could be leveraged in quantitative finance for analyzing lengthy financial reports, earnings call transcripts, or historical market data, where extracting relevant information from voluminous data is crucial. The improved accuracy and cost-efficiency over larger models could enable more scalable and cost-effective analysis in trading strategies.
title_cn: MEMENTO：面向长上下文处理智能体的上下文学习管理方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出的MEMENTO方法通过结合精细化调优和强化学习，显著提升了LLM智能体处理长上下文的能力。在量化交易领域，该技术可高效分析长篇财务报告和历史市场数据，以更低成本实现接近大型模型的性能，为基于文本数据的交易策略提供新的技术路径。

title: Structural Dual Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Primal-dual methods enforce safety constraints in reinforcement learning through Lagrangian relaxation. For a fixed policy, the exact bounded multiplier response exhibits bang-bang switching at the constraint boundary. Practical gradient updates can oscillate through coupling with policy optimization. We propose Structural DuaL Adaptation (SDLA), which replaces this bang-bang response with a unique continuous response through current-cost centering, trajectory weighting, and quadratic regularization. We characterize activation thresholds and response sensitivity. Ternary search computes multipliers without a dual gradient stepsize. For entropy-regularized tabular policies, we bound equilibrium constraint violations alongside reward gaps. We establish convergence of delayed updates under mild assumptions. Neural PPO/SAC experiments on OmniSafe and HASARD demonstrate competitive rewards with improved constraint tracking. On HASARD, PPO-SDLA achieves higher reported mean reward than the human baseline in six of eighteen settings while meeting the respective mean-cost budgets, including four with lower mean cost. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of higher mean reward at lower mean cost than the human baseline across multiple HASARD settings.
core_methodology: Proposes Structural DuaL Adaptation (SDLA) for safe reinforcement learning, which improves constraint satisfaction in policy optimization through current-cost centering, trajectory weighting, and quadratic regularization. Replaces traditional bang-bang multiplier responses with a continuous dual adaptation mechanism.
data_sources: Tested on OmniSafe and HASARD benchmarks (not financial datasets directly but methodology is transferable to trading environments)
alpha_potential: The improved constraint satisfaction mechanism could enhance risk-control in automated trading strategies by: 1) Better maintaining portfolio risk budgets 2) Preventing hazardous over-leverage 3) Ensuring regulatory/execution constraints are met during live trading
title_cn: 安全强化学习的结构双重自适应方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出SDLA算法，通过成本中心化和二次正则化改进强化学习中的约束满足。在量化交易场景下，该方法能更精确地控制策略风险敞口，在保证收益的同时严格满足风险预算，适合高频交易或组合优化中的动态风控需求。

title: HieraNTP: Structured Risk Representations for Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction
summary: Time-series anomaly detection commonly converts deviations from learned temporal regularities into anomaly scores. This practice can conflate violations of temporal regularity with task-specific anomaly judgments: the same deviation may be anomalous under one task definition and benign under another. Aggregating heterogeneous deviations into a single score before task-specific adaptation can obscure the evidence needed to distinguish these cases. We introduce HieraNTP, a Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction framework that separates self-supervised predictive modeling from task-specific risk interpretation. HieraNTP pretrains a hierarchical tokenizer and a causal next-token predictor to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales. It then organizes prediction discrepancies into a structured risk representation, preserving complementary evidence across temporal scales in token, local-statistic, and observation spaces. A task-adaptive detector uses anomaly labels to select and combine this evidence for the target task. Across anomaly detection benchmarks, HieraNTP improves VUS-PR by 12.0% on TSB-AD-U and 15.5% on TSB-AD-M relative to the strongest baselines, and achieves the highest composite score on both TAB tracks, with controlled comparisons supporting the value of retaining distinct evidence. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/HieraNTP.
core_methodology: Hierarchical next-token prediction framework with separate predictive modeling and task-specific risk interpretation, utilizing a hierarchical tokenizer and causal next-token predictor to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales.
data_sources: Time-series anomaly detection benchmarks (TSB-AD-U, TSB-AD-M, TAB tracks).
alpha_potential: Potential to identify nuanced market anomalies by separating temporal regularity violations from task-specific anomalies, useful for detecting structural breaks or abnormal market behaviors across different time scales.
title_cn: HieraNTP：通过分层下一令牌预测构建结构化风险表示的时间序列异常检测
summary_cn: HieraNTP通过分层令牌化和因果预测模型在多时间尺度捕获市场规律，并将预测差异组织为结构化风险表示。该方法在异常检测任务中表现优异，可有效区分不同任务定义的异常行为，为高频交易和风险监控提供新工具。

title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
summary: This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.
core_methodology: Entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for continuous-time consumption-investment problem under regime-switching market models with general utility functions. Utilizes randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization to derive closed-form optimal strategies (multivariate Gaussian for investment, Gibbs measure for consumption). Features a q-learning framework with theoretical guarantees.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to regime-switching market models (e.g., hidden Markov models for market regimes), though specific data sources not mentioned. Compatible with standard financial time-series (prices, macroeconomic indicators for regime detection).
alpha_potential: Exploits market regime dependencies through dynamic optimization. Key alpha sources: 1) Adaptive exploration of strategies across regimes 2) Theoretical optimality in stochastic control setting 3) Convergence guarantees to classical solutions. Particularly valuable for: - Multi-regime portfolio allocation - Crisis period hedging - Utility-aware wealth management
title_cn: 熵正则化强化学习在状态转换消费-投资问题中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种连续时间的熵正则化强化学习框架,用于状态转换市场模型下的消费-投资组合优化。通过理论推导得出封闭形式的最优投资(多元高斯分布)和消费策略(Gibbs测度),为多市场状态下的自适应资产配置提供算法支持。数值实验验证了学习方法在状态转换环境中的稳定收敛性,对量化对冲基金的动态资产配置策略开发具有实用价值。

title: AgentCBO: Causal Belief Routing for Bayesian Optimization under Unknown Graphs
summary: Causal Bayesian optimization (CBO) typically relies on the unrealistic assumption of a perfectly known causal graph. Recent methods relax this constraint by coupling optimization with structure learning, but they often waste sample budgets on structural uncertainties that are irrelevant to the optimizer. In this paper, we formalize routing-equivalence to shift the objective from full causal-graph recovery to causal belief routing, where structural differences only matter when they alter optimizer-facing objects such as admissible exploration sets and do-priors. Furthermore, we propose agentcbo, a graph-belief routing framework that incorporates LLM causal priors through guarded proposal and commit mechanisms. Specifically, a Language-Prior Agent combines LLM beliefs with constraint-based discovery to extract a protected causal backbone alongside residual uncertain edges. A Calibration Agent and a Residual Repair Agent then refine only these uncertain structures through score-gated bounded local edits. Finally, a deterministic commit gate evaluates candidate updates using routing-proxy checks before allowing them to influence intervention selection. Across ten benchmarks, agentcbo performs comparably to known-graph CBO, demonstrating that guarded LLM priors can improve fixed-budget CBO performance.
core_methodology: A causal Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates LLM causal priors through guarded proposal and commit mechanisms. It focuses on causal belief routing rather than full causal-graph recovery, refining uncertain structures through score-gated bounded local edits.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but typically involves simulated or real-world optimization benchmarks. Potential for financial data such as asset returns, factor exposures, or market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to optimize trading strategies by identifying causal relationships in market data, potentially uncovering non-obvious dependencies that can be exploited for alpha generation. The use of LLM priors could enhance the discovery of these relationships.
title_cn: AgentCBO：未知图下基于因果信念路由的贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合LLM因果先验的贝叶斯优化框架，通过因果信念路由而非完整因果图恢复来优化决策。在交易策略优化中，该方法可识别市场数据中的因果依赖，潜在提升策略表现。

title: FinForesight: A Diagnostic Backtesting Benchmark for Deep Research Systems in Financial Forecasting
summary: Anticipating financial outcomes requires synthesizing evolving evidence and reasoning under uncertainty, making deep research systems promising tools for forecasting. Yet evaluating forecasting ability is challenging because historical backtests may reward memorized outcomes or information retrieved after the forecast date. Live forecasting avoids direct access to realized outcomes, but feedback arrives only after events resolve. To obtain timely feedback and assess historical scores, we introduce FinForesight, a diagnostic backtesting benchmark for financial deep research systems. Across the Chinese, U.S., and Hong Kong markets, the benchmark evaluates four forecasting tasks: valuation, return ranking, event direction, and future financial fundamentals. Two capability diagnostic tasks assess counterfactual reasoning and financial calculation, scored separately from forecasting performance. Our harness-compatible framework restricts retrieved evidence to information available at the forecast date. We compare pretraining-era, resolved post-cutoff, and live evaluations to test whether controlled backtests approximate future performance. Pretraining-era scores exceed post-cutoff scores in most temporal comparisons, and stronger retrieval controls narrow the gap between post-cutoff backtests and live results. Forecasting attribution and robustness analyses reveal how scores respond to retrieval policy and how predictions respond to prompt rewrites and numerical perturbations. The code and benchmark data are publicly available.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a diagnostic backtesting benchmark (FinForesight) for deep research systems in financial forecasting. It evaluates forecasting tasks such as valuation, return ranking, event direction, and future financial fundamentals. The methodology includes controlling for information available at the forecast date and comparing pretraining-era, post-cutoff, and live evaluations to assess forecasting accuracy.
data_sources: The benchmark covers the Chinese, U.S., and Hong Kong markets, focusing on financial forecasting tasks and capability diagnostics like counterfactual reasoning and financial calculations.
alpha_potential: The benchmark aims to improve the reliability of financial forecasting by mitigating issues like memorization of historical outcomes or access to post-forecast information. This could lead to more robust forecasting models that generate alpha by better synthesizing evolving evidence and reasoning under uncertainty.
title_cn: FinForesight：金融预测深度研究系统的诊断回测基准
summary_cn: FinForesight是一个诊断回测基准，用于评估金融预测深度研究系统的性能。它通过限制预测日期可用的信息，避免历史结果记忆和事后信息的影响，从而提升金融预测的可靠性。适用于中美港市场，涵盖估值、回报排序、事件方向和未来财务基本面四项预测任务。该方法可用于改进量化交易中的预测模型。

title: HQNN-CL: Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Neural Network with Continual Learning for Financial Forecasting
summary: Financial time-series forecasting is still difficult owing to the non-stationary nature of the market, regime changes, and catastrophic forgetting, which makes conventional deep learning models hard to adapt in the long term. To achieve uncertainty-aware robust financial forecasting in the face of changing market conditions, this study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Continual Learning (HQNN-CL). The proposed framework combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) based regime detection, BiLSTM temporal encoding, adaptive-depth parameterized quantum circuits, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), experience replay, and probabilistic forecasting in a single architecture. The framework was tested on four real-time stock datasets: Microsoft, Systems Limited, Teradata and Tata Consultancy Services, and compared with seven state-of-the-art forecasting models, including recurrent and Transformer-based models. The experimental results show that HQNN-CL has outperformed other methods on the Systems Limited (RMSE = 3.0149) and Teradata (RMSE = 0.8909) datasets and is within 0.32% and 0.40% of the best baseline method for Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services, respectively. The proposed framework also generates well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts within the range of 89.5% to 96.5% empirical coverage rate, has zero catastrophic forgetting (BWT = 0.0000) for all sequential learning tasks, and consistently shows positive forward transfer. Ablation and statistical significance analyses also validate the performance of adaptive quantum feature learning and continual adaptation under heterogeneous market conditions, regime-wise.
core_methodology: Combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for regime detection, BiLSTM for temporal encoding, adaptive-depth parameterized quantum circuits, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), experience replay, and probabilistic forecasting in a hybrid quantum-classical neural network framework.
data_sources: Tested on four real-time stock datasets: Microsoft, Systems Limited, Teradata, and Tata Consultancy Services.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to adapt to changing market conditions and avoid catastrophic forgetting suggests potential for generating robust trading signals in non-stationary markets. The probabilistic forecasting and regime-aware features could be valuable for risk management and dynamic strategy adjustment.
title_cn: HQNN-CL：具有持续学习的混合量子神经网络用于金融预测
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合量子计算和持续学习的混合神经网络框架，通过市场状态检测和自适应量子特征学习，在非平稳市场中实现稳健的金融时间序列预测。实验表明其在多种股票数据上优于传统方法，并具有零灾难性遗忘特性，适用于动态交易策略的长期优化。

title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
summary: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. Perhaps unexpectedly, preliminary evidence has recently shown that existing single-table FMs (aka TFMs), when combined with suitable parameter-free relational encoders, can be quite competitive in practice despite zero exposure to RDB pre-training or relational data of any kind. In this work we first empirically confirm this phenomenon with a more diverse array of experiments. We then turn to our main contribution, namely, surfacing multiple complementary explanations for why TFMs behave so effectively. These explanations ultimately hinge on innate synergies whereby parameter-free encoders map relational effects to fixed-length embeddings that loosely mimic distributions for which TFMs were originally designed; in so doing, desirable single-table properties transfer to relational settings (e.g., convergent posterior predictive distributions). Collectively, our analysis forges new pathways for improving RDB FMs, particularly when we prioritize interpretability and inevitable integration within agentic systems.
core_methodology: The paper explores the use of single-table foundation models (TFMs) combined with relational encoders for predicting missing or future values in relational databases, without requiring RDB-specific pre-training. The methodology focuses on in-context learning and the mapping of relational effects to fixed-length embeddings.
data_sources: Relational databases (RDBs) storing heterogeneous tabular information, which could include financial time series, market data, or economic indicators in a structured format.
alpha_potential: The approach could be adapted to generate predictive signals from multi-table financial datasets, such as combining fundamental data with market prices for improved forecasting or anomaly detection in trading strategies.
title_cn: 为何表格基础模型在未见过的关系数据上表现出色
summary_cn: 本研究揭示了单一表格基础模型结合关系编码器在关系数据库预测任务中的有效性，无需特定预训练。该方法通过上下文学习将关系效应映射为固定长度嵌入，可能适用于金融多表数据预测，如基本面与市场数据结合的信号生成。

title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that current models exhibit distinct and systematic patterns of miscalibration that standard metrics often obscure. We further analyze common post-hoc recalibration methods and characterize which forms of calibration they can improve and which tend to persist. Our results provide practical guidance for evaluating and improving uncertainty calibration in TSFMs and highlight important limitations of current practice.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a taxonomy for how Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) represent predictive uncertainty and develops a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting. It distinguishes between pooled, horizon-wise, and conditional notions of calibration. The study evaluates popular TSFMs empirically and analyzes post-hoc recalibration methods.
data_sources: The study uses diverse datasets, though not explicitly financial, the methodology is applicable to financial time series data such as stock prices, volatility, and other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The research provides practical guidance on evaluating and improving uncertainty calibration in TSFMs, which can enhance the reliability of probabilistic forecasts in trading strategies. Better-calibrated uncertainty estimates can lead to more robust risk management and improved decision-making in algorithmic trading.
title_cn: 评估概率时间序列基础模型中的不确定性校准
summary_cn: 本文研究了时间序列基础模型(TSFMs)中不确定性校准的可靠性,提出了细粒度的评估框架并分析了常见后校准方法。研究结果为改进金融时间序列预测的不确定性校准提供了实用指导,可增强算法交易策略的风险管理和决策可靠性。尽管使用非金融数据集,方法论可直接应用于股票价格、波动率等市场指标的预测。

title: AIDA: An AI Outage Registry with Evidence from On-Chain MEV
summary: Generative AI coding tools have lowered the cost of writing trading software, but no systematic dataset records when these services fail. We introduce the AI Incident and Disruption Archive (AIDA), a multi-vendor registry of 5,868 deduplicated outage incidents across 30 providers from 2025 to 2026, with foundation-model incidents verified against primary status-page or postmortem URLs. Pairing AIDA with 5,041,034 verified maximal extractable value (MEV) transactions by 8,516 Ethereum addresses, their contract creations, and a 22-month Base Layer-2 panel of 1,099,593,191 swaps and 29,120 private executors, we establish two findings. First, entry into MEV expanded where code and public state suffice, as active arbitrage addresses quadrupled from late 2024 to late 2026 and liquidators grew by a third, while sandwich attackers, who need private order flow and builder access, declined. Execution nonetheless remained concentrated, with the top fifty addresses executing two thirds of verified trades. Second, AI outages stall new trading code while deployed bots keep trading. On Ethereum, addresses releasing a private executor fall to 0.67 on the day of an eight-hour disruption (0.68 for executor creations during OpenAI outage hours) and to 0.66 at lag two before rebounding on day three; on Base, operator top-level creations fall to 0.76 during OpenAI hours and executor-deploying operators to 0.88 at lag two. Non-trading creations, automated factory clones, and live arbitrage and sandwich execution across both chains remain unchanged. Cheaper code thus lowers the barrier to building MEV contracts, while private order flow, latency and capital still determine who wins execution.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AIDA, a registry tracking AI outages in trading software deployment, and pairs this data with on-chain MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) transaction data to analyze market impacts. The study specifically examines how AI service disruptions affect the creation and execution of trading bots, particularly in the Ethereum and Base Layer-2 ecosystems.
data_sources: The study utilizes two primary data sources: 1) AIDA registry with 5,868 AI outage incidents from 30 providers (2025-2026), and 2) On-chain Ethereum data including 5,041,034 MEV transactions, contract creations, and a comprehensive panel of swaps and private executors from Base Layer-2.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies quantifiable impacts of AI service outages on MEV strategies: 1) The barrier to entry for MEV contracts is lowered by easier coding access, but execution concentration persists among top players. 2) AI outages temporarily reduce new bot deployments while existing bots continue operating. This creates potential alpha through: - Identifying periods of reduced competition in MEV strategies during/after outages - Understanding how AI tool availability affects market participant behavior - Potential predictive signals from monitoring AI service status for MEV opportunities
title_cn: AIDA：基于链上MEV证据的AI故障登记系统
summary_cn: 本研究通过建立AI故障登记系统(AIDA)并结合链上MEV交易数据，系统分析了人工智能服务中断对量化交易策略部署的影响。研究发现：1)AI工具降低了MEV合约开发门槛，但执行仍高度集中；2)AI中断期间新交易机器人部署减少，但已有机器人持续运行。这为量化交易提供了重要启示：监控AI服务状态可作为MEV策略的潜在信号源，且在AI中断时期可能存在竞争减少的交易机会。

title: Learning AI Agents, Market Makers, and Stress in Automated Markets
summary: Automated markets increasingly route order flow from learning trading agents through automated market makers (AMMs). We model trader archetypes as AI agents defined by their reward functions and analyze the feedback they create on a constant-product AMM. Herd-dominated and arbitrage-dominated markets of equal size have identical return distributions and turnover, so no rule based on volatility, value-at-risk, stress frequency, or volume can tell them apart; yet their stress episodes differ in length by a factor unbounded in the feedback-to-noise ratio $\beta/s$. Serial statistics identify the feedback sign from $\Theta((s/\beta)^2\log(1/\delta))$ observations, and this rate is tight. When agents trade together, profit-seeking agents ride herds rather than lean against them, leading to all-or-nothing participation. Spread-earning market makers restore stability but make liquidity fragile, with discontinuous collapse and hysteresis; maker--taker pricing, not a uniform fee, is the effective instrument.
core_methodology: The paper models different trader archetypes (herd-dominated and arbitrage-dominated) as AI agents with specific reward functions and analyzes their impact on constant-product Automated Market Makers (AMMs). It focuses on feedback mechanisms in automated markets and the resulting market stress dynamics, using serial statistics to identify feedback signs.
data_sources: Theoretical and simulated data on constant-product AMMs, focusing on order flow and market behavior under different AI agent interactions.
alpha_potential: Provides insights into the stability and fragility of liquidity in automated markets, potentially identifying profitable strategies around herd behavior and market maker actions. Highlights the importance of maker-taker pricing in maintaining stability.
title_cn: 学习AI代理、做市商与自动化市场中的压力
summary_cn: 本文通过将不同交易者类型建模为具有特定奖励函数的AI代理，分析了它们在常数乘积自动做市商（AMM）上的反馈效应。研究发现，尽管 herd-dominated 和 arbitrage-dominated 市场的回报分布和成交量相同，但压力事件持续时间差异显著。套利代理倾向于跟随 herd 行为而非对抗，而做市商定价策略对市场稳定性至关重要。这些发现对量化交易中流动性管理和套利策略具有实际指导意义。

title: Reduced Cost Influence Functions for Predict-then-Optimize under Noisy Data
summary: Machine learning models deployed in decision-making pipelines, from vehicle routing to dynamic pricing to clinical decision support, must remain reliable in the face of low-quality training data. We study a predict-then-optimize setting in which an upstream model predicts the cost vector of a downstream linear program, with a large pool of noisy training data supplemented by a small curated set of clean data. We introduce Reduced Cost Influence Functions (RCIFs), which combine influence functions from robust statistics with the geometry of linear optimization to estimate how each training point shifts downstream decisions. Building on this, we propose a reweighting algorithm that uses RCIFs to downweight harmful training points and reduce downstream regret. Experiments on random linear programs and shortest-path problems show that our approach reduces regret, and accompanying theory characterizes properties of RCIFs and identifies regimes favorable to our method relative to baselines.
core_methodology: Combines robust statistics (influence functions) with linear optimization to identify and downweight noisy data points affecting downstream decision-making
data_sources: Large noisy datasets supplemented with small curated clean datasets (analogous to market data with different quality tiers)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve trading strategy robustness by filtering low-quality market data points affecting portfolio optimization, dynamic pricing, or routing decisions
title_cn: 噪声数据下预测后优化的降成本影响函数
summary_cn: 该研究提出结合鲁棒统计与线性优化的新方法，通过降低噪声数据权重提升决策模型稳健性。在量化交易中可应用于：1）脏市场数据过滤 2）组合优化稳定性增强 3）高频交易信号清洗，特别适用于存在不同质量层级的另类数据源处理场景。

title: Multiclass Classification with Rare Useful Features: Fundamental Limits and the Optimality of Diversity Pursuit Higher Criticism Thresholding
summary: We consider classification in high-dimensional feature spaces where only a vanishing fraction of features are useful and the number of classes may be large. While this rare-and-weak useful-feature regime is well understood in the binary setting, its multiclass version raises new questions: a feature can be useful for class discrimination without separating any specific pair of classes. We focus on a rare feature diversity model, in which most features are useless, but a small fraction promote discrimination among classes in a way that can be detected by a per-feature diversity test, such as one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test. For this setting, we propose Diversity Pursuit Higher Criticism Thresholding (DP-HCT), a feature-screening procedure that applies a higher-criticism threshold to the collection of p-values obtained from per-feature diversity tests. We justify DP-HCT under a Gaussian multiclass Rare-and-Weak Useful Feature model with class-mean contrasts of fixed magnitude in random directions, extending the binary model of Donoho and Jin (2008). When the number of classes is fixed, our model recovers the binary phase transition. When the number of classes grows logarithmically with the number of features, however, we derive a new and strictly harder phase transition, driven by the growing degrees of freedom and their effect on the useful-feature tail rate. We show that whenever classification beyond chance is possible, DP-HCT with ANOVA, followed by a simple classifier based on similarity to class means, achieves asymptotically perfect accuracy. Experiments on real multiclass classification benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements, and numerical simulations confirm that the derived phase-transition curve accurately predicts the finite-sample behavior of DP-HCT in the growing-class regime.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Diversity Pursuit Higher Criticism Thresholding (DP-HCT), a feature-screening procedure that applies higher-criticism thresholding to p-values from per-feature diversity tests (e.g., ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis test). It focuses on multiclass classification in high-dimensional spaces where only rare features are useful for class discrimination.
data_sources: The methodology is general and could be applied to financial data such as high-dimensional market data, alternative data (e.g., news sentiment, order flow), or factor-based features where only a small subset of features are predictive.
alpha_potential: DP-HCT could be valuable for identifying rare but predictive features in financial datasets, particularly in scenarios where most features are noisy or irrelevant. This aligns with challenges in factor investing, anomaly detection, or regime-switching models where only a few features matter at any given time. The method's robustness in high-dimensional settings makes it suitable for modern quantitative finance applications.
title_cn: 多类分类中的稀有有效特征：基本极限与多样性追踪高阶批评阈值的最优性
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种在高维特征空间中进行多分类的方法（DP-HCT），适用于金融数据中仅少数特征具有预测性的场景。该方法通过高阶批评阈值筛选特征，可有效识别市场中的稀有但重要信号，适用于因子投资、市场状态识别等量化交易应用。

title: Interpretable Allocation and Model-Predictive Rebalancing of Equity Portfolios, Tested on Real and Synthetic Markets
summary: A live equity portfolio poses three problems: which stocks to hold, when to trade, and whether the strategy holds up beyond the observed market. We built one system for all three and tested it on 373 US equities, calibrated on 2014-2024 and traded from January 2025 to September 2026. A selection rule chose stocks by score, by a bandit, or at random, and one of seven weighting rules, four consumer-theory utilities, and three standard portfolios, set share counts under limits on budget, single-stock weight, portfolio volatility, and turnover, with each stock's preference weight a bounded score of its trend, market beta, and the market's recent direction. A model-predictive controller forecasts portfolio value with a multi-asset geometric Brownian motion and re-planned at its horizon, when the value left its forecast band, or at a drawdown stop. To probe deeper declines than the real window held, we also ran the system on simulated markets from per-asset hidden Markov generators with jumps, linked by market and sector factors. On real prices, the stocks chosen mattered more to terminal wealth than the weighting rule, and the early re-plans shrank the worst drawdown in most rule combinations against a fixed calendar without consistently raising wealth. In the deepest simulated declines, every combination, random picks included, ended above simulated SPY and the equal-weight universe in the median, even without early re-plans, so the margin came from shared parts of the system, not from stock selection or re-plan timing. A market hedge that tightened a beta cap as the market weakened cost wealth on real prices but paid off in the most sustained simulated declines, and the generator's persistent trends favored score-based selection more than the real market did, which suggests a synthetic test judges stock selection fairly only if its generator does not build in that persistence.
core_methodology: Combines stock selection rules (score-based, bandit, random) with various weighting methods (consumer-theory utilities, standard portfolios) and employs model-predictive control for rebalancing based on forecasts from a multi-asset geometric Brownian motion model, tested on both real and synthetic market data.
data_sources: Historical data of 373 US equities from 2014-2024 for calibration, live trading data from January 2025 to September 2026, and synthetic data generated by per-asset hidden Markov models with jumps linked by market and sector factors.
alpha_potential: The system demonstrates alpha potential through its selection and weighting methodology, particularly in synthetic market conditions where persistent trends favor score-based selection. Early re-planning reduces worst drawdowns without consistently raising wealth, indicating risk management benefits.
title_cn: 可解释的股票分配与模型预测再平衡：在真实与合成市场中的测试
summary_cn: 该系统整合股票选择、权重分配和模型预测再平衡，通过多资产几何布朗运动模型预测投资组合价值，并在真实和合成市场中进行测试。结果显示，股票选择对终端财富影响较大，而早期再平衡能显著降低最大回撤。在深度模拟衰退中，该系统表现优于模拟SPY。

title: Achieving Exponential Asymptotic Optimality in Average-Reward Restless Bandits without Global Attractor Assumption
summary: We consider the infinite-horizon average-reward restless bandit problem. We propose a novel two-set policy that maintains two dynamic subsets of arms: one subset of arms has a nearly optimal state distribution and takes actions according to an LP-Priority routine; the other subset of arms is driven towards the optimal state distribution and gradually merged into the first subset. We show that our two-set policy is asymptotically optimal with an $O(\exp(-C N))$ optimality gap for an $N$-armed problem, under the assumptions of aperiodic-unichain, non-degeneracy, and local stability. Our policy is the first to achieve exponential asymptotic optimality under the above set of easy-to-verify assumptions, whereas prior work either requires a global attractor assumption or only achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. We further discuss obstacles in weakening the assumptions by demonstrating examples where exponential asymptotic optimality is not achievable when any of the three assumptions is violated. Notably, we prove a lower bound for a large class of locally unstable restless bandits, showing that local stability is particularly fundamental for exponential asymptotic optimality. Finally, we use simulations to demonstrate that the two-set policy outperforms previous policies on certain restless bandit problems and performs competitively overall.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel two-set policy for restless bandit problems, combining an LP-Priority routine for near-optimal actions with a dynamic merging strategy to gradually improve state distributions. The approach achieves exponential asymptotic optimality under verifiable assumptions (aperiodic-unichain, non-degeneracy, and local stability).
data_sources: The methodology is theoretical and simulated but could be applied to financial data where sequential decision-making is required, such as dynamic asset allocation or market-making strategies.
alpha_potential: This approach could be adapted for multi-armed bandit problems in trading, such as dynamic portfolio optimization, where arms represent different assets or strategies. The exponential convergence could lead to more efficient resource allocation in high-frequency or algorithmic trading contexts.
title_cn: 在不依赖全局吸引因假设的情况下实现平均收益型多臂老虎机问题的指数级渐近最优
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新型的两集合策略，通过动态管理资产子集和LP优先策略，在满足易验证假设条件下实现了指数级渐近最优。这一方法为高频交易和动态资产配置中的资源分配问题提供了理论支持，可应用于量化交易中的多策略优化场景。

title: Non-Convex Market Makers: Coherence without Convexity, Friction, and Parallel Composition
summary: Cost-function market makers are always assumed convex, and convexity is not what makes them coherent. For a path-independent maker the exact no-arbitrage condition is a chord condition, that every chord slope of the cost lie in the convex hull of payoffs; convexity enters the standard axiomatics through a separate requirement, monotone information incorporation, and dropping it leaves coherent non-convex makers. Rational flow against such a maker trades the convex envelope, so non-convexity costs expressiveness rather than soundness, and a proportional fee of at least the arbitrage depth restores no-arbitrage, which by conjugation is a bid-ask spread with an exact no-trade interval for any cost whatever. Combining fee-bearing makers is an infimal convolution solved by one monotone clearing-price root-find, with sparse participation and a consolidated limit order book as the aggregate, and a deep quadratic co-quoter is Moreau smoothing, which preserves coherence at every depth. Any quoted configuration outside the coherent hull admits a portfolio priced below its worst payoff, so arbitrageurs act as decentralized separation oracles, and coherence is relative to friction and to the cost of finding certificates.
core_methodology: The paper introduces non-convex market makers that maintain coherence without requiring convexity, focusing on path-independent market makers and no-arbitrage conditions. It explores how rational flow trades the convex envelope and how proportional fees can restore no-arbitrage. The methodology also includes combining fee-bearing makers through infimal convolution and discusses the role of arbitrageurs as decentralized separation oracles.
data_sources: Theoretical market maker models, limit order books, and arbitrage conditions. No specific real-world data sources are mentioned, but the framework can be applied to any market with a limit order book structure.
alpha_potential: The paper's framework could potentially be used to design more efficient market maker algorithms that better handle non-convex payoffs and arbitrage conditions. This could lead to improved liquidity provision strategies and better handling of complex derivative products. The discussion on arbitrageurs acting as decentralized separation oracles also hints at potential new ways to detect and exploit arbitrage opportunities.
title_cn: 非凸市商：无需凸性、摩擦和平行构成的相干性
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种非凸市商模型，在不依赖凸性条件下保持相干性，研究了路径无关市商的无套利条件及合理流动性管理。通过费用机制恢复无套利状态，并探讨了组合市商的卷积方法。对量化交易中市商算法设计和套利检测具有实践指导意义。

title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
summary: Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(\lambda^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.
core_methodology: Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) applied to regularized CVaR portfolio optimization, addressing discontinuous stochastic gradients and dimension-independent convergence properties.
data_sources: Simulated Gaussian portfolios (in experiments), applicable to real-world asset returns data.
alpha_potential: Potential for improved risk-adjusted returns through more stable CVaR optimization under non-smooth conditions, especially in high-dimensional portfolios where traditional methods struggle with dimension-dependent performance degradation.
title_cn: SGLD的非渐近分析及其在组合CVaR最小化中的应用：间断随机梯度的新途径
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于随机梯度朗之万动态的新方法，用于解决条件风险价值优化中因非光滑损失结构导致的维度依赖问题。通过几何结构分析和维度无关常数设计，实现了更稳定的高维组合CVaR优化，实验验证了其在模拟数据下的优越性能。

title: Optimal portfolio and consumption under no-shorting constraints: The exploratory formulation and reinforcement learning
summary: We develop a reinforcement-learning framework for the continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption via utility maximization under no-shorting portfolio constraints. We adopt the exploratory formulation under entropy regularization and impose no-shorting constraint through a componentwise nonnegative conditional-mean constraint on the class of admissible randomized policies, while the sampled actions are allowed to be negative during the training. For CRRA utility, we derive the homothetic value function and the optimal Gaussian portfolio and Gibbs consumption policies under some model conditions and establish a verification theorem. These results allow compatible parameterizations in actor, critic, and $q$ functions for a constrained policy-iteration algorithm. Policy evaluation uses trajectory-based moment conditions, and policy improvement uses fitted coefficients to solve a convex quadratic program over the nonnegative orthant without requiring market coefficients as inputs. The mean constraint preserves tractable Gaussian exploration throughout parameter learning, while modal deployment converts the learned randomized policies into deterministic controls. In particular, the Gaussian mode coincides with its constrained mean and hence satisfies no-shorting constraint, and the Gibbs mode determines the deployed consumption rule.
core_methodology: The paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption problems with no-shorting constraints. It uses an exploratory formulation under entropy regularization and employs randomized policies with Gaussian exploration during training. The approach involves a constrained policy-iteration algorithm with actor-critic methods and parameterized functions, converting learned randomized policies into deterministic controls for deployment.
data_sources: The methodology is model-agnostic in terms of market data inputs, suggesting it can be applied to various financial assets and time series data, though specific data sources are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The framework can potentially generate alpha through optimized portfolio allocation and consumption strategies under realistic trading constraints (no-shorting), adapting to market conditions via reinforcement learning. The Gaussian exploration and entropy regularization may help in discovering robust strategies in varying market regimes.
title_cn: 禁止卖空约束下的最优投资组合与消费：探索性公式与强化学习
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一个强化学习框架，用于解决连续时间下禁止卖空约束的最优投资组合和消费问题。通过熵正则化和随机策略探索，采用高斯策略进行参数学习，最终转换为确定性控制策略。该方法无需输入市场系数，具有直接应用于量化投资组合管理的潜力。

title: Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model
summary: This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows for interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings. We propose the Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method that integrates LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to simultaneously perform variable selection and model specification. Theoretically, we establish that S-LASSO possesses oracle properties in terms of selection consistency and asymptotic normality. Monte Carlo simulations confirm that S-LASSO outperforms existing alternatives across a variety of scenarios. Empirically, we apply S-LASSO to a characteristics-based asset pricing model, exploring the linear and nonlinear effects of asset-specific characteristics on cross-sectional returns, as well as their interactions with firm size.
core_methodology: Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method integrating LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to perform variable selection and model specification for high-dimensional semiparametric models.
data_sources: Asset-specific characteristics (presumably from CRSP/Compustat or similar fundamental data) and cross-sectional returns.
alpha_potential: Explores nonlinear effects and interactions between firm characteristics and size in asset pricing, potentially uncovering new factors or characteristic combinations that explain cross-sectional returns.
title_cn: 规范LASSO与基于特征的灵活的资产定价模型
summary_cn: 本研究提出规范LASSO方法，可同时进行变量选择和模型设定，应用于资产定价领域，有效分析公司特征对收益的非线性影响及与规模的交互作用，为多因子策略开发提供了新的计量工具。

title: Generating Financial Time Series by Matching Random Convolutional Features
summary: Generating realistic financial time series is challenging as training data is often limited to a single historical path. With such scarce data, overfitting is hard to avoid, especially under adversarial training where a trained discriminator can memorize the training samples. To mitigate this, recent approaches train generators to minimize the discrepancy between untrained feature representations of real and generated time series. In these works, the feature maps are based on path signatures, which can fail to capture relevant time series properties at tractable truncation depths. In this work, we instead train generators by matching random convolutional features of real and generated time series. Existing random convolutional feature maps, such as Rocket and Hydra, have been shown to provide informative representations of real-world time series, but cannot supervise generative models because they are non-differentiable. We introduce SOCK (SOft Competing Kernels), a fully differentiable random convolutional feature map, suited to train generative time series models. We show that generators trained by matching random SOCK features outperform signature and diffusion baselines on most evaluation metrics across a wide range of small-sample financial datasets. We further demonstrate SOCK's expressiveness on two-sample hypothesis testing and time series classification tasks, where SOCK matches or outperforms existing unsupervised feature maps.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SOCK (SOft Competing Kernels), a fully differentiable random convolutional feature map, to train generative time series models by matching features of real and generated financial time series. This approach addresses the challenge of overfitting in adversarial training by using untrained feature representations.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on a wide range of small-sample financial datasets, though specific datasets are not named in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The ability to generate realistic financial time series with limited historical data can enhance backtesting and strategy development, particularly in scenarios where data scarcity is a concern. This could lead to improved model robustness and better generalization in trading strategies.
title_cn: 通过匹配随机卷积特征生成金融时间序列
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种名为SOCK（软竞争核）的全可微分随机卷积特征映射方法，用于通过匹配真实和生成时间序列的特征来训练生成模型。该方法在少量金融数据上表现优异，优于现有基准方法，可用于增强回测和策略开发，特别是在数据稀缺的情况下。

title: The Inference-Compute Frontier for Limit Order Book Prediction
summary: We identify an empirical inference-compute frontier for limit order book prediction on FI-2010. A power law fitted to low- and mid-compute models extrapolates to an excluded MLPLOB-style mixer family whose work is $56$--$2{,}515$ times the largest budget in the corresponding fit. Across nine folds and five horizons, pooled $R^2$ is $0.934$ on the realized target frontier, with 59\% lower RMSE than constant endpoint extrapolation, and $0.731$ on all excluded operating points. Measured latency gives a weaker relationship and reorders model families. We therefore design FastBiNLOB to pack computation into dense temporal and feature mixing. H120 exceeds the published state-of-the-art macro-F1 on two of four horizons in every one of five seeds. Under our CPU/MPS protocol, H96 reduces median latency by 23.6\% relative to the W128 MLPLOB reference, and H120 by 60.2\% relative to a TLOB-inspired dual-axis attention reference.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on optimizing the inference-compute trade-off for limit order book prediction, utilizing a power law model for extrapolation and introducing FastBiNLOB for dense temporal and feature mixing to improve computational efficiency and latency.
data_sources: FI-2010 dataset, which is a benchmark dataset for limit order book prediction.
alpha_potential: The methodology could improve the speed and accuracy of limit order book predictions, potentially leading to better execution strategies and reduced latency in high-frequency trading environments.
title_cn: 限价订单簿预测的推理-计算前沿
summary_cn: 该研究通过优化限价订单簿预测中的推理与计算权衡，提出了一种基于幂律模型的推断方法，并设计了FastBiNLOB算法以实现高效的时序和特征混合。在FI-2010数据集上的实验表明，该方法在预测准确性和计算延迟方面优于现有技术，对高频交易中的执行策略优化具有潜在价值。

title: Agentic AI in Automated Markets
summary: Automated markets increasingly host autonomous, learning trading agents and are powered by formulaic automated market makers (AMMs). We study how heterogeneous agent behavior shapes stress, risk-adjusted performance, liquidity, and volatility in these types of markets. Three behavioral archetypes are modeled as agentic reinforcement learning (RL) systems: a rational arbitrageur, a manipulator, and a retail herd-follower. Each archetype is defined by its reward function within a common, asset-agnostic exposure-control environment, and each is trained with a value-based Deep Q-Network (DQN) and with REINFORCE using a learned baseline. A pilot on hourly cryptocurrency data (AAVE, ETC, SUI) motivates the hypotheses. Herd-followers produce the most frequent but shortest stress episodes, manipulators the fewest but most persistent, and rational agents the most stable rolling Sharpe ratios despite higher return volatility.
