core_methodology: Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) with a two-phase approach: initial reward estimation across different dynamics followed by active selection of dynamics to reduce reward uncertainty
data_sources: Expert demonstrations (potentially simulated trading strategies or historical trades)
alpha_potential: Could help identify robust reward functions that transfer across different market regimes, potentially improving strategy adaptation to changing conditions
title_cn: 通过主动逆向强化学习推断可迁移的奖励函数
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种主动逆向强化学习方法，通过智能选择动态环境来减少学习可迁移奖励函数所需的专家演示数量。在量化交易中，该方法可帮助开发适应不同市场状态的稳健交易策略，减少对大量历史交易数据的需求。

title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. We propose an axiomatic framework that derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry and Linearity), treating them as structural constraints rather than heuristic design choices. This formulation builds on a novel NAHT decomposition, which characterises the fundamental difference between open and fully controllable multi-agent systems, and establishes a cooperative game-theoretic foundation for learning. We further show that enforcing these axioms on learning individual value functions recovers the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs, providing a principled bridge between reinforcement learning and classical cooperative game theory. Building on this framework, we introduce Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, two generic algorithmic templates that can be instantiated with standard reinforcement learning methods. When applied to strong base algorithms such as IPPO and POAM, our methods consistently improve learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types and conventions across NAHT benchmark tasks. The code of experiments is published on https://github.com/hsvgbkhgbv/axiomatic-rl-naht.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an axiomatic framework for reinforcement learning in open multi-agent systems, leveraging Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry, and Linearity) to derive value function learning. It introduces Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines as algorithmic templates that can be instantiated with standard reinforcement learning methods.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on benchmark tasks for n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), which could be adapted to financial market simulations or multi-agent trading environments.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to improve learning efficiency and generalization to unseen agent types could be valuable in developing adaptive trading strategies that perform well in dynamic market conditions with multiple interacting agents. The cooperative game-theoretic foundation may help in modeling market participant interactions and identifying strategic advantages.
title_cn: 开放多智能体系统中强化学习的公理化框架
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一个基于Shapley公理（效率性、对称性和线性）的强化学习公理化框架，适用于开放多智能体系统。通过引入Shapley Machines和Banzhaf Machines两种算法模板，该框架能提升学习效率和对未见智能体类型的泛化能力，可应用于动态金融市场中多智能体交易策略的开发。

title: Bridging Neural Tangent Kernel Analysis and Reinforcement Learning for Deep Function Approximation
summary: Despite their widespread success across machine learning, the learning dynamics and generalization properties of neural networks remain poorly understood. The neural tangent kernel (NTK) provides an analytical characterization of the learning dynamics of infinitely wide neural networks and serves as a useful proxy for finite-width networks in supervised learning. In this work, we extend the NTK framework to reinforcement learning (RL) by introducing a temporal-difference (TD) flow formulation that accommodates time-varying mini-batches and TD targets, yielding a closed-form solution for value function evolution in an overparametrized setting. We also devise an optimization-based state-space exploration method that leverages the closed-form solution, coupled with constraints on the environment, to model the set of feasible states. On a deterministic grid environment, we validate that the proposed RL-based NTK formulation is indeed learning efficiently and adapting to the distribution shift in the training data distribution, and we demonstrate that the resulting exploration strategy improves sample efficiency. To our knowledge, this is the first work to extend NTK theory to characterize the learning dynamics of RL training with time-varying mini-batches and TD updates.
core_methodology: Extension of Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) framework to Reinforcement Learning with Temporal-Difference (TD) flow formulation for value function evolution in overparametrized settings
data_sources: Theoretical analysis validated on deterministic grid environment (synthetic data)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving RL-based trading strategies through better understanding of learning dynamics in neural networks, particularly in adaptive exploration and distribution shift handling
title_cn: 连接神经正切核分析与强化学习以进行深度函数逼近
summary_cn: 本研究将神经正切核理论扩展至强化学习领域，提出了带有时变小批量训练和时间差分目标的TD流框架，为过度参数化情况下的值函数演化提供闭式解。这一理论基础可应用于改进RL交易策略的学习效率和分布偏移适应，但需进一步验证真实市场数据下的表现。

title: A Bayesian Framework for Safe Optimal Control of Unknown Systems from Input-Output Data
summary: As control engineering is applied to increasingly complex systems, learning-based control, which uses empirical data to reduce the reliance on first-principles models, has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, such approaches must cope with nonlinear and stochastic dynamics, the absence of state measurements, and scarce data, while ensuring safe operation under constraints, which requires rigorous uncertainty quantification. Whereas existing methods treat these challenges in isolation, this article proposes a Bayesian framework that jointly addresses them. A prior in state-space form is updated from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, yielding a representation of joint uncertainty over dynamics and latent states. Building on this representation, a validation procedure is developed that provides probabilistic guarantees for constraint satisfaction under arbitrary causal control laws. For control synthesis, a formulation penalizing the conditional value-at-risk of the constraint function is proposed, together with an adaptive calibration mechanism that adjusts the performance-robustness trade-off to achieve a desired robustness level. The probability of successful certification is characterized theoretically. The framework is extended to a receding-horizon setting, where posterior updates from new measurements allow the controller to progressively reduce uncertainty and improve performance. The approach is demonstrated on the optimal control of a vertical farm.
core_methodology: Bayesian framework for updating state-space priors from input-output data using particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, with robust control synthesis focusing on conditional value-at-risk of constraint functions.
data_sources: Generic input-output data (could be adapted to market data feeds or trading signal inputs)
alpha_potential: Potential application in automated trading systems where safe operation under constraints is required, particularly in risk management and adaptive execution strategies
title_cn: 基于输入输出数据的未知系统安全最优贝叶斯控制框架
summary_cn: 本文提出的贝叶斯框架通过输入输出数据更新状态空间先验，采用条件风险价值约束的鲁棒控制方法，可应用于量化交易中的自适应执行策略和风险控制系统，在数据稀缺环境下提供概率安全保证。

title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
summary: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.
core_methodology: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model (ST-GFM) combines Chebyshev filters, bidirectional diffusion filters, and temporal attention for graph-based forecasting. Features include Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR) and perturbation bounds for robustness.
data_sources: Evaluated on METR-LA and PEMS-BAY datasets, which likely represent traffic sensor networks (common benchmark datasets for spatiotemporal forecasting).
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial networks (e.g., cross-asset correlation forecasting) given its handling of shifting graph structures and spectral-temporal dynamics. The perturbation bounds suggest robustness to market regime changes.
title_cn: ST-GFM：具有测量扰动边界和掩蔽谱重构的时空图预测模型
summary_cn: ST-GFM通过切比雪夫滤波、双向扩散滤波和时序注意力机制实现时空图预测，其扰动边界理论和掩蔽谱重构技术对金融网络的动态相关性建模具有潜在价值。该框架对市场状态变化的鲁棒性可能适用于跨资产动量策略或风险因子预测。

title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
summary: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.
core_methodology: Uses a large language model (LLM) to automate the tuning of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver parameters by analyzing solver logs and proposing configuration edits based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior. The approach includes a regime-adaptive objective and log-based completion signal to optimize solver performance.
data_sources: Solver logs from MIP solver runs on 215 instances from five benchmark sets.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve the efficiency and performance of optimization algorithms used in portfolio optimization, trading strategy development, and other quantitative finance applications that rely on MIP solvers. The method could reduce the time and computational resources required to find optimal solutions.
title_cn: 基于日志驱动的语义调优对混合整数规划求解器的改进
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种利用大型语言模型（LLM）自动调优混合整数规划（MIP）求解器参数的方法，通过分析求解器日志并提出配置建议，显著提高了求解器的性能。这一方法在量化金融中，尤其是在投资组合优化和交易策略开发方面，具有潜在的应用价值，可以减少寻找最优解所需的时间和计算资源。

title: Pricing Today, Shaping Tomorrow: Contextual Dynamic Pricing in Purchase-Driven Evolving Systems
summary: Across diverse markets, it is important for firms to balance attracting customers with managing operational conditions, such as workloads and delivery times. Dynamic pricing plays a central role in this tradeoff, as the orders generated today can change the conditions faced by future customers. We develop a novel framework for contextual dynamic pricing with an observed shared state and unknown purchase-driven transitions. The valuation model allows unknown mean functions of customer covariates and state, unknown state-specific scales and a common unknown standardized noise distribution. We propose Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems (SHAPE), which incorporates a purchase's future revenue consequences into current pricing. Purchase-shadow adjustment and scale standardization reveal a common one-dimensional oracle price map across states, allowing SHAPE to retain its pricing history across value updates without repeating coarse exploration. The same active sales records support price-map learning and joint updates of continuation values and purchase shadows, without fitting the noise distribution or full transition matrices. To support this reuse under purchase-driven feedback, we establish pricing guarantees for history-dependent inputs and stability bounds for the joint updates. Under regularity, coverage and design conditions, we obtain sublinear expected regret against a finite-horizon dynamic oracle for linear, H\"older and sparse linear mean models. For affine valuations at fixed state and feature dimensions, SHAPE matches the static semiparametric minimax time exponent up to logarithmic factors for every fixed noise-tail smoothness order $\beta\ge2$. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the appealing performance of SHAPE.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SHAPE (Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems), a contextual dynamic pricing framework that incorporates future revenue consequences into current pricing decisions. It uses purchase-shadow adjustment and scale standardization to maintain a common oracle price map across states, enabling efficient learning and updates without full transition matrices or noise distribution fitting.
data_sources: The framework is designed for markets where customer purchases and operational conditions (e.g., workloads, delivery times) are observable. It leverages customer covariates and shared state information, though specific data sources are not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: SHAPE's ability to dynamically adjust prices based on both current and future conditions could be adapted for algorithmic trading in markets with similar dynamics, such as limit order book management or inventory-based trading strategies. The method's sublinear regret guarantees suggest robust performance in evolving market conditions.
title_cn: 今日定价，塑造未来：购买驱动演化系统中的情境动态定价
summary_cn: 该研究提出SHAPE框架，通过将未来收入影响纳入当前定价决策，实现情境动态定价。其购买阴影调整和规模标准化方法可维持跨状态的统一价格映射，适用于需平衡客户吸引与运营条件的市场，对算法交易中的动态定价策略具有潜在应用价值。

title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
summary: Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem. We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a fairness-aware contextual bandit framework with Lipschitz fairness constraints, which includes a lazy fair greedy algorithm for continuous contexts and a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm for general context distributions. These methods ensure fairness at every round while optimizing regret.
data_sources: Synthetic and real data, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for fair algorithmic trading strategies, ensuring equitable treatment of different market segments while optimizing returns. The regret bounds suggest efficient learning of decision boundaries in high-dimensional contexts.
title_cn: 公平感知上下文多臂老虎机中的最优学习
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种公平感知的上下文老虎机框架，通过Lipschitz公平约束确保相似上下文的个体获得相似的动作分布。该方法可优化遗憾并减少决策边界的维度，适用于高维上下文环境。虽然在金融数据上的直接应用未明确提及，但该方法有望用于设计公平且高效的交易策略。

title: Principled Human-AI Collaboration in Agentic Workflows
summary: Organizations adopting AI face the challenge of deciding which outputs can be released without human review while meeting the quality standards of human experts. We develop a statistical framework for delegating tasks between experts and black-box generate-verify workflows, in which AI-generated answers are verified and revised over multiple rounds. Before deployment, human experts evaluate selected outputs, and their judgments are used to calibrate the verifier threshold and number of attempts. Our method selects the policy with the highest estimated automation rate among statistically approved candidates, without modifying the generator or verifier. We establish finite-sample control of the error rate among released outputs, characterize the expert evaluations sufficient to attain a target automation rate, and derive a minimax lower bound establishing rate optimality in the quality margin and required confidence. In a MultiHiertt financial question-answering case study, average held-out automation increases from 2.50% to 24.17% as expert evaluations accumulate, while released-output error rates remain around 1.20%. In contrast, heuristics that release answers after consistently high verifier scores either violate the 5% error tolerance or automate at most 1.30% of tasks. Synthetic experiments further examine these theoretical predictions under controlled settings.
core_methodology: Statistical framework for delegating tasks between humans and AI in generate-verify workflows, optimizing verifier thresholds and number of attempts based on expert evaluations
data_sources: MultiHiertt financial question-answering dataset (specific financial QA data not detailed), synthetic experiments
alpha_potential: Potential to automate parts of financial decision-making workflows with controlled error rates, applicable to areas like earnings analysis or news interpretation
title_cn: 基于原则的人类-AI在代理工作流中的协作
summary_cn: 该论文开发了一种统计框架，用于在金融问答等场景中优化人类与AI的协作流程，实验显示可将自动化率从2.5%提升至24.1%同时保持1.2%的错误率。对量化交易中需要人工复核的决策流程（如新闻解析、财报分析）的自动化改进具有参考价值。

title: Beyond Imputation: Mask-Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Tree Embeddings on General Missing Data Mechanisms
summary: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free framework for uncertainty quantification with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. Yet, missing values introduce distributional heterogeneity, where marginal coverage can hide systematic undercoverage for certain missingness patterns. At the same time, existing methods based on distances or smoothness require a continuous representation of partially observed covariates. Although imputation restores continuity, it obscures the missingness patterns and introduces task-dependent overhead. We develop a new CP framework that is \emph{adaptive to missingness patterns}, without imputing covariates. We rely on data augmentation by feature embedding that accounts for missingness. Our framework represents each input with missing values by a tree embedding together with its raw missingness mask, and then learns a regularized quantile score function. Varying the choices for the penalty function and the augmentation enables us to characterize three practically relevant validity levels: exact coordinate-wise validity, exact validity on observed masks, and approximate missingness-conditional guarantees for general mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support these guarantees and show that the proposed method reduces miscoverage risk while maintaining informative intervals, especially in non-MCAR settings. These results highlight the practical value of uncertainty quantification that adapts to missingness.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a conformal prediction framework that adapts to missing data patterns without imputation, using tree embeddings and regularized quantile score functions to provide uncertainty quantification with different validity guarantees.
data_sources: The method is tested on synthetic and real datasets, suggesting potential applicability to financial datasets with missing values.
alpha_potential: The framework could improve risk assessment and decision-making in trading strategies by providing more accurate uncertainty quantification in the presence of missing data, particularly in non-MCAR settings where missingness is not random.
title_cn: 超越插补：基于树嵌入的缺失数据通用机制下的掩码自适应共形预测
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的共形预测框架，通过树嵌入和缺失掩码直接处理缺失数据，无需插补，从而在不同缺失机制下提供更准确的不确定性量化。对于量化交易，该方法可提升在数据缺失情况下的风险模型准确性，尤其在非随机缺失场景中具有实际应用价值。

title: Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games
summary: This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.
core_methodology: Discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, using optimization formulations and learning algorithms including fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods.
data_sources: Theoretical frameworks applied to various scenarios such as crowd motion, traffic routing, and epidemic management, suggesting potential application to market behavior and agent-based modeling.
alpha_potential: Could be adapted for modeling large populations of algorithmic traders or market participants, with potential insights into optimal trading strategies in high-frequency or liquid markets.
title_cn: 离散时间平均场博弈的优化框架与学习算法
summary_cn: 本研究介绍了有限状态和行动空间的离散时间平均场博弈，并探讨了其优化公式和学习算法。该方法适用于研究大型市场参与者的近似均衡行为，可能为高频交易或流动性市场的策略优化提供理论基础和实现算法。

title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
summary: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.
core_methodology: Reinforcement learning with constraints on rare catastrophic events using large deviations principle and cumulant generating functions (CGFs) to upper bound failure probabilities
data_sources: Generic Markov decision processes (can be adapted to financial time series data)
alpha_potential: Potential for developing robust trading strategies that avoid catastrophic losses by maintaining proper risk constraints even in extremely rare market conditions
title_cn: 基于大偏差理论的罕见事件约束强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种强化学习方法，利用大偏差理论和累积量生成函数来约束极端罕见但破坏性事件的发生概率，在量化交易场景中可应用于设计规避黑天鹅风险的投资策略。

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
summary: We compare three zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, 8192-hour context, no covariates) with the Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM baselines, with their code and hyperparameters unchanged, for 96-hour forecasts of hourly carbon intensity in the Nordic bidding zones NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4. The design, the analysis code and a minimum detectable effect (MDE) were timestamped before any foundation-model forecast by an OpenTimestamps proof (Bitcoin-confirmed) and the GPG-signed tag prereg-v1; the proofs are archived in Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23881315). The preregistration was also submitted to OSF Registries 2026-11-02 07:49 UTC (osf.io/hncz5; embargo requested, pending OSF approval). On the 2025 test (361 daily origins, contamination not ruled out) all three models have a lower zone-averaged MAPE than both baselines, by 0.952 to 1.347 percentage points (Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction, all p < 0.0001), and each beats SARIMA in 9 of 9 zones. On a post-release holdout of 14 origins from 2026-10-16 the point estimates have the same sign (0.729 to 1.326 percentage points lower), but all lie within the preregistered MDE of 2.989 points and are reported as not determined. For calibration (RQ4) the preregistration locked a Diebold-Mariano-HLN test on CRPS; the MDE applies to MAPE only. Holdout CRPS point estimates (n = 14) are 1.1114 (Timestral-5M), 1.0733 (Timestral-209M) and 1.1198 (Chronos-2) against 1.4165 gCO2-eq/kWh for SARIMA (each p < 0.0001). The SARIMA quantiles are constructed from the fitted model's Gaussian predictive distribution (deviation D-03), not taken from a native v1.5 forecast, so the difference may partly reflect the SARIMA intervals. The contamination indicator does not exceed its preregistered threshold for any comparison; with 14 holdout origins it has low power (HAC standard errors 0.124 to 0.360 pp).
core_methodology: Comparison of zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M, Chronos-2) against traditional SARIMA and GBM baselines for 96-hour carbon intensity forecasts.
data_sources: Hourly carbon intensity data from Nordic bidding zones NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4.
alpha_potential: Potential for improving forecasting accuracy of carbon intensity, which could indirectly benefit energy trading strategies and ESG-focused portfolios.
title_cn: 零样本时间序列基础模型与Khepri v1.5基准在九个北欧竞价区96小时碳强度预测中的预注册对比
summary_cn: 本研究比较了三种零样本时间序列基础模型与传统SARIMA和GBM模型在北欧竞价区碳强度预测中的性能。结果表明基础模型在预测精度上显著优于传统方法，可能对能源交易和ESG投资策略中的碳强度预测提供更准确的输入。

title: EventGPT: Next-Event Pretraining on Banking Customer Histories
summary: A model pretrained to predict a customer's next event can estimate the probability of future events without training on their labels and provide a reusable representation for supervised downstream banking tasks. We pretrain EventGPT, a hierarchical causal transformer, by next-token maximum likelihood estimation on the public Multimodal Banking Dataset (MBD-mini: 100,224 clients, 38.8 million transactions and 66.3 million geolocation pings). Keeping one state per event, EventGPT trains in about two hours on one L4 GPU at windows up to 8,192 tokens. From its next-event distribution, with no labels, EventGPT scores five targets of the form "the client makes a transaction of a given kind for the first time next month" at ROC-AUC 0.79 to 0.92. Gradient boosting on 114 engineered features needs 10,000 to 300,000 labeled client-months to match it on four targets and stays below it on the fifth. For product prediction, frozen EventGPT embeddings score below the engineered features (mean ROC-AUC 0.787 against 0.808 over five test folds), and a rank-averaged ensemble of EventGPT, profile fields and token counts with the engineered features adds 0.014 to 0.017, of which 0.007 to 0.016 is EventGPT's own. The code and pretrained weights are released.
core_methodology: EventGPT is a hierarchical causal transformer pretrained using next-token maximum likelihood estimation to predict a customer's next event in banking transactions. It provides a reusable representation for supervised downstream tasks without requiring labeled data for training.
data_sources: Public Multimodal Banking Dataset (MBD-mini) with 100,224 clients, 38.8 million transactions, and 66.3 million geolocation pings.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to predict future customer transactions and events without labeled data could be leveraged for behavioral finance strategies, customer segmentation, and predictive analytics in financial services. The ensemble approach combining EventGPT with engineered features shows incremental performance improvements.
title_cn: EventGPT：基于银行客户历史的下一个事件预训练
summary_cn: EventGPT是一种分层因果Transformer模型，通过无监督学习预测银行客户的下一个事件，可用于未来交易概率估计和行为分析。在金融交易中，该模型可用于客户行为预测和产品推荐，结合传统特征工程可进一步提升预测性能。

title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
summary: We consider nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the intensity function of a Poisson process, allowing the intensity to depend on observed covariates. Such models describe how event rates vary with external conditions, including conditions under which the intensity becomes arbitrarily small or vanishes. However, risk analysis based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence typically requires the true intensity to be bounded away from zero, a restrictive assumption in applications. We develop a unified approach that avoids this assumption and derive an oracle inequality for the covariate-averaged Hellinger distance between the true intensity and the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE). As an application of the oracle inequality, we establish convergence rates for NPMLEs based on deep neural networks (DNNs). Our results show that, as in nonparametric regression, the ability of DNNs to capture underlying structure leads to improved convergence rates. Specifically, DNN-based NPMLEs mitigate the curse of dimensionality when the true intensity has a compositional structure and automatically adapt to a low-dimensional Riemannian manifold structure of the event space. For intensity functions with a compositional structure, DNN-based NPMLEs achieve nearly minimax-optimal convergence rates without explicitly incorporating this structure into the network architecture. Simulations demonstrate that DNN-based estimators outperform kernel estimators in most settings, while manifold kernels remain competitive in some designs. Finally, we analyze stimulus-evoked neural spiking using data from the Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels project. DNN-based NPMLEs provide better out-of-sample performance than a conditional kernel estimator, as evaluated by held-out log-likelihood.
core_methodology: Nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of Poisson process intensity functions using deep neural networks (DNNs), allowing for covariate-dependent intensity estimation without requiring the intensity to be bounded away from zero.
data_sources: Simulated data and neural spiking data from the Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels project. Potential adaptation to financial event data (e.g., trades, orders, news events).
alpha_potential: Method could be adapted to model event arrival rates in financial markets (e.g., trade executions, news arrivals, order book events) where intensity varies with market conditions. The DNN's ability to handle compositional structures could capture complex market regimes.
title_cn: 基于深度学习的协变量驱动泊松过程非参数强度估计
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种使用深度神经网络进行泊松过程强度非参数估计的方法，可处理协变量依赖且强度趋零的情况。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于建模市场事件（如交易、新闻）的到达强度，捕捉不同市场条件下的复杂模式，潜在提升事件驱动策略的预测能力。

title: Over-fitting Control in Deep Nonlinear Matrix Completion via Gradual Nonsmooth Regularization
summary: Conventional matrix completion methods exploit the underlying low-rank structure of a target matrix to recover its missing entries, but may be inadequate for capturing complex nonlinear dependencies. Deep neural networks have therefore been increasingly adopted for nonlinear matrix completion (NLMC). However, their high representational capacity, particularly in deep fully connected neural networks (FCNNs), can lead to over-fitting when training is restricted to incomplete observations. In this paper, we propose a Deep Neural Network with Nonsmooth Regularization (DNN-NSR) framework to address this issue by incorporating two complementary structural priors: sparsity of intermediate representations and low-rankness of layer-wise weight matrices. Specifically, the $\ell_1$-norm of hidden representations promotes sparse latent features, while the nuclear norm of weight matrices encourages low-rank layer-wise transformations. To optimize the resulting nonsmooth and nonconvex objective, we develop an extrapolated proximal gradient algorithm that employs soft-thresholding and singular-value thresholding to handle the two regularization terms, respectively. We further introduce a gradual regularization strategy that progressively increases the influence of these structural penalties during training. Under suitable assumptions, we establish convergence properties of the proposed algorithm toward a critical point of the training objective. The effectiveness of DNN-NSR is evaluated through extensive experiments on synthetic matrix recovery, single-image inpainting, and recommender systems using the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets. Comparisons with representative linear and nonlinear matrix completion methods demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to improve recovery performance by jointly exploiting sparse latent representations and low-rank network transformations.
core_methodology: Deep Neural Network with Nonsmooth Regularization (DNN-NSR) framework incorporating sparsity of intermediate representations and low-rankness of layer-wise weight matrices to prevent over-fitting in nonlinear matrix completion.
data_sources: Synthetic matrix recovery, single-image inpainting, and recommender systems using the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve recovery of missing data in financial time series or cross-sectional asset data by capturing complex nonlinear dependencies while controlling over-fitting, which could enhance signal extraction in quantitative models.
title_cn: 通过渐进非光滑正则化控制深度非线性矩阵补全中的过拟合
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合稀疏潜在表示和低秩网络变换的深度神经网络框架，通过非光滑正则化控制过拟合。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于修复缺失的市场数据或提取资产间的非线性关系，提升因子模型的稳健性。

title: Learning to Charge More: How Q-Learning Firms Lock In Supracompetitive Prices
summary: There is growing experimental evidence that $Q$-learning agents can learn to charge supracompetitive prices. We ask when such behavior persists, whether it emerges, and which strategies support it. In a repeated pricing game in which firms condition on the previous period's price profile, we give conditions on the learned action values under which supracompetitive prices become an absorbing state once experimentation ends. We then show that under softmax exploration these conditions are reached with positive and explicitly bounded probability, both from a random and from an all-zero initial $Q$-table. In the latter case firms lock in supracompetitive prices because they never learn that undercutting pays; the same mechanism can lock in the competitive price, so the long-run outcome is selected by the exploration path. Finally, we give sufficient conditions on the learned table under which the induced strategy is naive collusion, a grim trigger strategy or an increasing-price strategy; grim trigger strategies are subgame perfect under a standard discounting condition, whereas naive collusion is generally not an equilibrium.
core_methodology: Q-learning in repeated pricing games, examining strategies that lead to supracompetitive pricing through reinforcement learning and game theory
data_sources: Theoretical game setups, not using real-world market data
alpha_potential: Potential insights into algorithmic collusion behaviors which could inform regulatory strategies or detect abnormal market coordination in trading environments
title_cn: 学习抬高价格：Q-学习公司如何锁定超高竞争价格
summary_cn: 本研究使用Q学习方法，在重复定价游戏中研究公司如何通过强化学习锁定超过竞争水平的价格。论文提供了在实验结束后维持高价的条件，以及实现的概率界限。这些发现对理解金融市场中算法的潜在共谋行为及设计相应的市场监管策略具有参考价值。

title: A Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering Framework with Automated Cluster Cardinality Estimation Ability
summary: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown. To address these limitations, we introduce in this paper the Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering (GSFC) framework, which incorporates a continuous sparsity penalty into the fuzzy objective function. Because closed-form solutions are precluded by the simultaneous presence of fuzzifier and sparsity exponents, we propose an efficient primal-dual bisection search coupled with specialized analytic pathways to rigorously enforce the partition constraint while organically driving trace memberships to exact zero. This mathematically enforced sparsity empowers the algorithm to autonomously estimate the true number of clusters by dynamically pruning redundant clusters, provided that it is initialized by a larger than the true number of clusters. Furthermore, we integrate a virtual noise sink to insulate outliers from the rest of the data points. The usage of the proposed framework is also extended to line segment detection. Extensive empirical evaluations across synthetic toy datasets, high-noise geometric stress tests, and real-world benchmarks (UCI wine dataset and hyperspectral images) demonstrate that GSFC effectively exceeds conventional fuzzy benchmarks while autonomously resolving cluster cardinality. Additionally, it significantly outperforms existing sparse possibilistic and probabilistic soft-clustering alternatives in line detection tasks.
core_methodology: Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering with automated cluster cardinality estimation and noise handling
data_sources: Synthetic toy datasets, high-noise geometric stress tests, UCI wine dataset, hyperspectral images
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying hidden patterns in noisy financial data, but not directly demonstrated for market data

title: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail
summary: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks. We design a posterior-sampling agent for it. Each period it draws a market from an exact posterior and posts the bid and discount of that market's exactly solved season plan, so every action is one a fully informed seller could take. In a simulated online florist it has the lowest regret averaged over markets. In weak markets it gives up 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons, four to seven times less than drawing once per season. A planner acting on point estimates can stop bidding and never learn that bidding pays. The agent escapes after about three seasons on average, against fifty with one draw per season. Where displayed scarcity keeps willingness to pay above the posted price, the discount needs no learning. Customers waiting for the discount to return to its recent level look like lost sales, so frequent waiting makes the agent underrate its market. One discount per season removes waiting at a cost of 5.9% of clairvoyant revenue in a weak market and none in a strong one.
core_methodology: Posterior-sampling agent for dynamic pricing and bidding in online retail
data_sources: Simulated online florist data (sponsored-search clicks, sales data with perishable products)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability to financial markets, but potential insights for dynamic pricing strategies in similar contexts

title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
summary: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. Early-stopping methods aim to stop once enough reasoning is available to answer. Evaluating these methods requires accounting for the cost of deciding when to stop and the reliability of the resulting answer. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol. We introduce Target-Integrated Token Efficiency (TITE) to measure efficiency relative to the oracle across accuracy targets. We also examine correctness at later exit positions, transfer across models and tasks, post-stop reasoning continuation, and retained justification quality. In our experiments, correctness can decrease at later positions beyond what the fitted decoding-noise model predicts. Reliability checks also reveal continued reasoning after forced termination and weaker supporting reasoning in some correct early-stopping outputs. The implementation can be found in https://github.com/hung20gg/audit-early-stopping.
core_methodology: Early-stopping methods for large reasoning models to optimize computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy
data_sources: Mathematical and scientific reasoning tasks, code generation, and factuality tasks
alpha_potential: Potential to optimize computational resources in AI-driven trading strategies, but direct financial application not demonstrated

title: Quantization of Large Models with Weight Outliers and Sparsity
summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the memory burden of large model deployment by casting the high precision trained weights to fewer bits. While this promotes memory-efficient inference, it also incurs quantization error that impairs model performance. To compensate for quantization error, the present contribution decomposes the original trained weights into a quantized matrix, a low-rank component, and a sparse matrix that accounts for outlier rows in the weights. Due to analytical intractability and the discrete structure of the decomposition, a simulated annealing search is employed to explore candidate decompositions while avoiding poor local minima. Numerical tests demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach across a broad suite of large language models, including Llama 3.2 1B, Llama 3.2 3B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen2.5 7B, evaluated on natural language generation benchmarks using 4-bit NF4 and FP4 quantizers. The novel method can markedly outperform direct quantization while incurring minimal memory overhead.
core_methodology: Post-training quantization with decomposition into quantized matrix, low-rank component, and sparse matrix for outlier rows, optimized via simulated annealing.
data_sources: Large language models (e.g., Llama 3.2 1B, Llama 3.2 3B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B) evaluated on natural language generation benchmarks.
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential; primarily focuses on model compression for inference efficiency rather than generating trading signals.

title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
summary: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions. Even so, a marginal test ranks expert-labelled direct above not-direct pairs within each action (AUROC 0.658) better than every null we built, so the panel does carry information about which pairs are direct. Tuned discovery methods, in configurations feasible at this panel size, recover less of it than a simple pairwise cross-correlation when pairs are ranked within each action, and no more when they are ranked within each target, which removes what the target alone predicts. Most direct pairs (132 of 222) involve actions below the support needed for 80% power against a 0.1-SD effect. For flow targets, conditioning on the target's other expert-labelled parents, often filed alongside the action, erodes the marginal discrimination, and most not-direct associations survive it: even with the graph's parent sets supplied, the expected separation does not emerge. For each property, we give a diagnostic computable before any discovery method is run.
core_methodology: Measurement of observable properties in causal discovery methods, focusing on constraints like tail behavior, random walk characteristics, and intervention rarity in corporate financial data
data_sources: US public firms (2,901 companies over 31 quarters) using SEC 8-K filings (71 corporate action types) and financial-statement items (11 metrics)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability - shows causal discovery challenges with real financial data, but methodology could inform preprocessing for alternative data analysis

title: Robustness Starts with the Objective: Designing and Certifying Robust LLM-Generated Heuristics
summary: LLMs are increasingly used to design heuristics for computer systems. However, most synthesis frameworks evaluate candidates by their average performance, which can mask severe regressions on specific workloads. Even adding adversarial training inputs doesn't eliminate these regressions, and percentile objectives (e.g., optimizing for the 95th percentile) overlook how severe regressions can be beyond the selected threshold. We present TAILOR, a framework that guides LLM synthesis using the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the cost difference between each candidate and an existing baseline on the same workload. This paired CVaR measures the average difference over the worst fraction of workloads. We show that a negative paired CVaR guarantees improvements in both average performance and tail optimality gap relative to the unknown optimum, without ever computing that optimum. We find that TAILOR achieves the best mean--tail trade-off among the synthesis objectives we evaluate across three case studies: Azure GPU batch admission, Azure VM packing, and server placement. Tested across seven diverse optimization benchmarks, TAILOR produces heuristics that are certified with 99% confidence to improve both average performance and tail optimality gaps over the baseline in six of them. On these six benchmarks, TAILOR also outperforms known robust, human-designed alternatives in the tail while achieving better or comparable average-performance improvement over the baseline.
core_methodology: Uses Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) to guide LLM synthesis for generating robust heuristics, focusing on tail performance improvements
data_sources: Computer system workloads (GPU batch admission, VM packing, server placement), no financial market data
alpha_potential: Method could potentially be adapted for developing robust algorithmic trading strategies in extreme market conditions, but no direct financial application demonstrated

title: Regularized Wasserstein Distance for Discrete Generative Modeling and Clustering Analysis
summary: In this paper, we formulate clustering analysis as discrete generative modeling. Specifically, when the generator is restricted to a finite candidate space, the generated samples naturally emerge as the most representative prototypes of the underlying data distribution. To model such a discrete candidate space, we employ a Discrete Distribution Network (DDN). However, DDN suffers from unstable training due to its hard nearest-neighbor selection. To stabilize training and encourage geometric consistency, we replace DDN's l2 loss between images with regularized Wasserstein distance between the empirical distributions of real and generated images. The resulting framework, termed Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC), offers four notable advantages: 1) the learned cluster centers are directly interpretable, as they are realistic synthetic samples; 2) the inference cost scales logarithmically with the number of clusters, i.e., O(log K), making the method scalable to extremely large K; 3) the regularized Wasserstein distance provides a smooth and well-behaved optimization objective that facilitates stable convergence, whereas DDN's l2 loss tends to converge to poor local optima; and 4) DGC replaces DDN's nearest-neighbor selection with random-neighbor selection, which avoids the density shift problem during multi-step forward. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and desirable properties of DGC. The code is publicly available at GitHub.
core_methodology: Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC) using regularized Wasserstein distance for prototype selection
data_sources: Generic benchmark datasets (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability to trading, though the clustering methodology could theoretically be adapted for market regime detection

title: Personalized Rollout Allocation for Federated LQR Policy Optimization under Heterogeneous Process Noise
summary: We study federated model-free learning of a common linear quadratic regulator (LQR) gain under a limited uplink communication budget, with clients that share dynamics and costs but experience different process-noise levels. Conventionally, clients transmit gradient matrices whose dimension equals the number of controller parameters. Exploiting the structure of two-point zeroth-order estimates, we consider an implementation in which clients transmit only one scalar cost-difference coefficient per rollout pair, while the server regenerates the associated perturbation directions from shared seeds. Communication thus scales with the number of rollout pairs rather than the controller dimension, turning the uplink budget into a rollout budget. Because noise heterogeneity produces gradient estimates of widely differing variance and every client carries equal weight in the fleet objective, uniform rollout allocation allows noisy clients to dominate the aggregated update and increases the probability of destabilizing updates. We propose a rollout-allocation scheme that assigns rollout pairs in proportion to the standard deviation of each client's estimates and show that it minimizes the variance of the aggregated update. The scheme is implemented exactly through a greedy integer allocation rule whose weights are estimated from the communicated scalars. We further prove that a single allocation factor quantifies its improvement over uniform allocation in a one-round instability bound, the certified step size, and the error floor of a joint stability and convergence guarantee. Simulations show that, under the same communication budget, personalized allocation reduces the one-step instability rate from $37\%$ to $0.3\%$.
core_methodology: Federated model-free learning of a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) gain with personalized rollout allocation to address heterogeneity in process noise.
data_sources: Simulated data with clients sharing dynamics and costs but experiencing different process-noise levels.
alpha_potential: Limited direct application to trading; potential for optimization in distributed control systems, but unclear translation to financial markets.

title: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis
summary: AI data analysis today is three fragmented worlds: LLMs understand semantics but cannot compute; BI aggregates precisely but is stateless; ML processes large-scale data on a stateful kernel but lacks semantics. This paper proposes a combination mechanism, named Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, that fills a still-open gap - the multi-engine joint context: the data context is embedded into LLM conversational analysis, where the LLM serves only as the semantic, reasoning, and orchestration layer (not computation) and connects four engines through the 1M context window - Python and R ML kernels, SQL over relational databases, Cypher over graph databases - yielding two multiplications, "semantics and precise computation" and "relational and graph", under enterprise-grade governance. The novelty is a four-dimensional coordinate system: horizontal (engine kinds), vertical (state flow - the watershed), spatial (business generalization), temporal (iterative convergence); a deterministic grounding method (one-shot injection of schema.json + notes.md, M+S) carries the spatial and temporal dimensions. Empirically, all four dimensions are substantiated: horizontally, four engines are quantified - SQL, Cypher (96.5% on CypherBench movie), ML in Python and R (TabReD weather); vertically, state flows across engines and grounding is reused across kernels; spatially, SQL generalizes across three business databases - AdventureWorks 91.3%, financial 95.3%, formula_1 94.6% (average), about 20-23 points above single-shot SOTA 74.45%; temporally, accuracy converges monotonically as notes accumulate. The core invariant - the separation of semantics from computation plus a cross-data-domain persistent context - does not expire as LLMs and agents evolve or engine forms change.
core_methodology: Multi-engine joint state data analysis combining LLMs for semantics and reasoning with computational engines (Python/R ML kernels, SQL, Cypher)
data_sources: Relational databases, graph databases, and structured data (e.g., financial databases, formula_1, weather data)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving data analysis workflows by integrating semantic understanding with precise computation, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: TreePIN$^{2}$: Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks
summary: Fitted decision trees provide predictive knowledge for neural network initialization. We present Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks (TreePIN$^{2}$), a method that translates split rules, decision paths and leaf predictions into initial network weights and biases for classification and regression. Sigmoid units encode split responses, hidden units combine them along decision paths, and leaf predictions initialize the output layer. We calibrate split softness using local training margins, sample support and impurity reduction, relating the initial responses to the data at each node. All weights and biases remain trainable, allowing gradient-based optimization to refine the transferred decisions and their combinations. Across six classification and six regression tasks with twenty paired seeds, TreePIN$^{2}$ improves mean initial and early validation performance over initialization baselines on most tasks. After fifty epochs, it achieves the best or tied-best mean validation performance among the six compared methods on ten tasks. Paired ablations show how split calibration and leaf-informed output initialization contribute to the starting predictor and its subsequent learning.
core_methodology: Method for initializing neural network weights using decision tree structures (split rules, decision paths, and leaf predictions)
data_sources: Generic classification and regression datasets (not financial-specific)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving model initialization in financial prediction tasks, but no direct trading application demonstrated

title: Efficient Conformal Calibration for Paired Recommendation Decisions
summary: Risk control can suppress useful changes to a frozen recommendation rule. We study how to recover valid activation from the same observed fractional losses. Two specified internal calibrators can lose efficiency by compressing losses into their sum or clipping auxiliary inverse counts before averaging. We propose Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration, or ACRC, which averages before clipping. A product identity proves expected-risk validity, while pointwise bounds characterize the additional activation. For fixed populations sampled without replacement, we connect activation to signed utility under heterogeneous users and switching constraints. Near the budgets, positive population mean gain and the stated nondegeneracy conditions give positive leading-order utility increments despite sampling dependence. Across six datasets, changing only calibration improves discounted net utility by $0.010226$ over raw and $0.008337$ over RB. A separately frozen Jester confirmation gives $0.011025 \pm 0.001082$ over raw with the rule and filter fixed, using a five-seed approximate 95 percent paired interval. Against information-matched SCoRE selecting risk or reward scores, the mean utility difference is $+0.015934 \pm 0.001440$. These gains use more mean realized risk within the declared budgets. Upstream failures delimit the benefit: efficient calibration releases useful modifications when the proposals themselves have value.
core_methodology: Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration (ACRC) for improving recommendation decisions by averaging before clipping losses
data_sources: Six unspecified datasets, including Jester confirmation data
alpha_potential: Potential for improving decision-making systems by better risk calibration, but not directly linked to financial markets

title: Robust Reward Machine Learning and Execution in Noisy Environments
summary: Background: Reward machines (RMs) represent non-Markovian reward functions as finite-state machines over high-level propositional events. Traditionally, these events are generated by a deterministic labelling function that maps environment states to proposition sets. However, real-world labelling functions are inherently noisy. Objectives: Design and implement a method that learns RMs in the presence of noisy labelling functions and exploits them for policy learning in both discrete and continuous environments. Methods: We propose Prob-IRM, a method that learns RMs from noisy proposition histories using inductive logic programming (ILP) and exploits them for policy learning. Noisy proposition histories are represented as training examples for ILP, which learns an RM that maximises coverage of low-uncertainty histories. RM learning is interleaved with policy optimisation. Prob-IRM uses a belief over RM states to determine when to relearn the RM and to provide additional guiding rewards. Results: Prob-IRM is evaluated on environments with discrete and continuous state spaces under varying levels of labelling noise. Prob-IRM performs comparably to baselines using handcrafted RMs and outperforms approaches that use recurrent neural networks to encode history, despite operating with noisy labels. Conclusions: Prob-IRM represents a step towards deploying reward machines in noisy, real-world environments.
core_methodology: Combines inductive logic programming (ILP) with RM learning to handle noisy inputs in reinforcement learning settings
data_sources: Abstract mentions 'environments with discrete and continuous state spaces' - no financial market data explicitly tested
alpha_potential: Potential to improve noisy signal interpretation in trading environments, but no direct financial application demonstrated

title: Do Earnings Calls Help Predict Financial Restatements? Evaluating Text Beyond Public Firm Information
summary: Financial restatements correct errors in previously published financial reports. Could managers' language in earnings calls warn of them in advance? Comparing 109 calls that precede restatements with 218 matched control calls, we find that the text predicts restatements but adds no detectable ranking gain beyond public firm information. A text classifier beats chance, largely because of restatements tied to special-purpose acquisition companies, but a model using only public information scores slightly higher. With refitting, the 95% interval for the gain from adding text (-0.05 to 0.11 AUROC) still leaves room for a meaningful benefit. A large language model scores higher, but we show that it names the exact ticker in 66% of masked transcripts, and it was released after the restatements occurred. Our results suggest that finding new warning signs in call text requires a public-information baseline and a check of what a language model already knows.
core_methodology: Text classification of earnings call transcripts to predict financial restatements
data_sources: Earnings call transcripts and public firm information
alpha_potential: Limited, as text analysis adds no significant predictive power beyond public information for most cases

title: World Models Need Not Be Right to Rank Policies Right: Relative Bounds and Audit Limits
summary: Selecting a reinforcement-learning (RL) policy usually requires additional environment interaction, while learned world models offer cheap but potentially biased evaluations. This raises two distinct questions: can shared model errors preserve pairwise rankings despite poor absolute values, and do they make a small number of real audits more informative? We derive an exact pairwise simulation identity and a relative bound separating common-mode Bellman residuals from policy-specific error. The analysis motivates RAVEL (Relative Auditing of Value Errors in Learned models), a selective policy tournament whose eliminations use held-out real outcomes. We test 45 SAC, TD3, and PPO policies per task in DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk. At rollout horizon 500, model rankings remain strong (Kendall tau = 0.962 and 0.800), and same-run differential-error ratios are 0.674 and 0.106. Yet mean paired audit-error correlations are only 0.007 and 0.090, and pairing changes standard deviation by -2.5 percent and +1.9 percent. Simultaneous intervals attain 99.98 percent and 99.75 percent coverage, but certify only 13.2 percent and 0 percent of decisions at eight audits. RAVEL improves low-budget walker-walk regret, whereas real-only successive halving is better at the largest budget, rejecting the precommitted twofold efficiency target. Frozen-model optimization lowers real return without increasing predicted return on average. Thus ranking fidelity, useful audit covariance, and upward model exploitation are distinct properties, separated in part by closed-loop trajectory divergence.
core_methodology: Relative ranking of RL policies using learned world models with selective auditing via real outcomes
data_sources: DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk simulations (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential methodology for adaptive portfolio strategy selection, but no direct financial application demonstrated

title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
summary: Relative-position attention mechanisms offer compelling alternatives to RoPE across various transformer architectures, delivering superior performance in domains such as audio. These mechanisms typically modify attention scores by adding content-position or bias-position terms. Unlike RoPE, which encodes position via per-token rotations directly on the queries and keys, relative-position terms generally require pairwise offset-dependent computation or lookups, complicating their integration into fused attention kernels and introducing severe memory, bandwidth, and compute overheads as sequences scale. To address this bottleneck, we propose an exact attention algorithm that incorporates additive relative-position terms into FlashAttention-style tiled computation. Our method (1) uses offset-aware tiling to avoid redundant indexing and memory accesses, (2) computes only the necessary key/query-relation products and reuses them across token pairs in both forward and backward passes, and (3) uses offset-based gradient sharding and aggregation, eliminating atomic contention. We provide a unified, efficient Triton implementation across diverse relative-position attention mechanisms and evaluate it against naive and specialized implementations. For 8K-token sequences, our method speeds up the forward (backward) pass by 1.8-6.4$\times$ (2.0-21$\times$) and reduces peak memory up to 2.9-128$\times$ (1.4-54$\times$) over the strongest baseline for each mechanism, enabling long-context end-to-end transcription that is 1.8$\times$ faster and uses 2.4$\times$ less memory. Our method thus provides a drop-in, hardware-efficient solution for scaling relative-position attention transformers.
core_methodology: Efficient computation of relative-position attention mechanisms in transformers using optimized tiling and memory management
data_sources: General sequence data (audio/text), not financial-specific
alpha_potential: Potential applications in NLP-based market sentiment analysis if adapted to financial text/transcripts, but no direct trading signals demonstrated

title: A Batched Hartigan's $k$-Means Clustering
summary: Hartigan's $k$-means algorithm has theoretical advantages over the standard Lloyd's variant, which has become synonymous with "$k$-means". Yet, Hartigan's algorithm is far slower in practice due to its inherently sequential calculations. We devise a Batched Hartigan's method that enables vectorized calculation by exploiting the triangle inequality to expose a set of parallel-safe updates and a smaller set of sequential updates. This makes Hartigan's method competitive with Lloyd's in execution speed for the first time.
core_methodology: Batched Hartigan's k-means clustering with vectorized calculations using triangle inequality
data_sources: Generic numerical data (not finance-specific)
alpha_potential: Potential for improved clustering in factor analysis or regime detection, but requires significant adaptation for financial data

title: Meta-memorization and memorization scaling laws in transformers
summary: Larger transformers can memorize more data, with a capacity (in bits) that scales roughly linearly with the number of parameters. Counterintuitively, larger models also memorize faster, requiring fewer repetitions of a sequence during training before it is memorized. We reproduce both memorization scaling laws in transformers trained on random binary sequences, showing that rapid memorization can arise even when data contain no semantic or compositional structure. Rapid memorization is due to a meta-memorization effect, where models trained to memorize a large set of random sequences learn to memorize novel sequences more quickly. The rate $r(t)$ at which models memorize grows with training time $t$ as a power-law $r(t) \sim t^{\beta}$ with a fixed exponent $\beta$ but an increasing upper cutoff across model scales. Meta-memorization enables even one-layer transformers to few-shot memorize a 100-bit sequence. This effect is partly explained by the formation of structured attention heads that convey position-invariant sequence information to MLPs where memorized sequences are stored. Meta-memorization is recapitulated in a simplified model of a dense associative memory where retrieval is constrained by an attentional bottleneck. Our results suggest transformers, through pre-training, acquire reusable mechanisms that enable highly efficient storage and retrieval of memories.
core_methodology: Investigation of memorization scaling laws in transformers using random binary sequences
data_sources: Random binary sequences (synthetic data)
alpha_potential: Potential indirect relevance through understanding transformer memorization capabilities, but no direct market application demonstrated

title: CREDO: Evidence-Conditioned Credit Assignment for Temporal Reasoning Agents
summary: Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering (TKGQA) requires language model agents to retrieve evidence, select relevant facts, and perform multi-step temporal reasoning. However, the trajectory-level outcome signal in GRPO does not explicitly distinguish the quality of intermediate decisions: downstream failures can penalize useful evidence acquisition, while identical rewards in all-failed groups eliminate the relative outcome signal despite differences in intermediate progress. We propose Credit Redistribution with Evidence-Driven Opportunities (CREDO), which uses intermediate evidence to recover local supervision, including in all-failed groups, and determine where outcome supervision acts. CREDO assigns positive stage-level credit through comparisons among rollouts of the same question and uses retained answer overlap as an opportunity proxy to shift part of the outcome-policy weight toward reasoning and answering. The framework preserves terminal rewards and trajectory-level advantages, while redistribution conserves total outcome-policy weight per trajectory. Following the public evaluation protocol of prior work, CREDO raises Overall accuracy from 78.0% to 82.4% and Multiple accuracy from 55.0% to 65.6% on MultiTQ relative to the strongest published baseline in our comparison. On TimelineKGQA, it raises cross-KG accuracy from 30.9% to 36.4% relative to our reproduced baseline via direct transfer to ICEWS Actor under matched training and evaluation settings.
core_methodology: Credit assignment via intermediate evidence for temporal reasoning in knowledge graph question answering
data_sources: Temporal Knowledge Graphs (likely non-financial domains)
alpha_potential: Potential indirect application in temporal pattern recognition but not directly applicable to market data

title: Yielding Fairness: Coupled Learning and Fairness for Value-Weighted Ranking
summary: Risk screening and recommendation systems pass or block accounts that generate both value and loss. Under a blocked-value budget, a cap on expected value forgone through blocking, the optimal ranking orders accounts by expected value per unit expected loss, a ratio of conditional expectations. This rule can conflict with accepted harm or net-harm criteria, blocking accounts that another criterion would pass at the same budget. We call these cases account-level objections and define group complaint disparity as the difference between groups' normalized realized objections. Weighted binary cross-entropy (W-BCE) implements the value-per-loss order with one score. Objection penalties modify the ranking, while group multipliers scale those penalties differently by group, tracing tradeoffs between loss capture and complaint disparity. This preserves the value-budgeted ranking structure and makes the cost of reducing contestable blocks explicit. Across public recommendation, insurance, credit, and mortgage datasets, we compare undamped W-BCE with ordinary BCE using yield Gini, an area summary of loss capture versus blocked value. Logarithmic weight damping is evaluated separately. Held-out evaluations measure capture-disparity tradeoffs. Validation-selected group-aware complaint penalties improve complaint closure in some cohorts. A corrected comparison normalizes and enlarges candidate policy banks using validation-only price sweeps and retains all ten applicable sources. The source-level results do not establish a statistically significant average advantage over group-blind pricing at the fixed minimum retained loss capture. We also compare with blocked-count, blocked-value, and protected-loss parity postprocessors, which do not directly constrain realized objections, and measure objections in candidate-count and loss units.
core_methodology: Weighted binary cross-entropy (W-BCE) with objection penalties and group multipliers to balance loss capture and fairness in ranking
data_sources: Public recommendation, insurance, credit, and mortgage datasets
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability; mainly focuses on fairness in value-loss tradeoffs rather than financial alpha generation

title: MatMoE: Matryoshka Mixture-of-Experts with Dynamic Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient Inference
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture has been widely adopted in large language models (LLMs) since it reduces the computational cost through sparse expert activation. However, the massive parameter scale of MoE models hinders their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Although existing mixed-precision quantization reduces the model size, they are inherently static, fixing the bit-width of each expert across decoding steps. Such static schemes yield suboptimal performance as they overlook the dynamic variation in expert importance during decoding. Furthermore, they fail to adapt to the dynamic latency constraint driven by the fluctuating system utilization. To address these challenges, we propose MatMoE, a dynamic mixed-precision quantization framework for efficient MoE inference. MatMoE features: (1) a Matryoshka MoE PTQ algorithm that enables experts to operate flexibly at multiple precisions within a stringent memory budget; (2) a floor-and-compensation quantization method that eliminates redundant memory accesses in the Matryoshka representation; and (3) a dynamic bit-width allocation strategy that determines the precision for each expert based on their routing scores to satisfy the dynamic latency requirement. We implement our MatMoE system atop llama.cpp for both CPU and GPU platforms. Extensive evaluations across three modern MoE models and challenging benchmarks demonstrate that MatMoE achieves $4.0\% \sim 18.3\%$ higher accuracy than state-of-the-art static mixed-precision method. Compared to llama.cpp, MatMoE delivers $1.3\times \sim 3.7\times$ speedup on Raspberry Pi 5, and $1.2\times \sim 1.3\times$ speedup on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Orin.
core_methodology: Dynamic mixed-precision quantization framework for efficient Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference
data_sources: Not specified (likely general LLM benchmarks)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving efficiency of large language models in trading applications, but no direct financial application demonstrated

title: CoGSeq-LTV: Scalable Missing-Aware Graph-Sequence Modeling for Multi-Business Transaction Analytics
summary: Large-scale super-apps generate heterogeneous transaction logs in which users interact with multiple businesses, item identifiers are only partially available, and future value targets are sparse, heavy-tailed, and cumulative over time. We study multi-business, multi-horizon value prediction as a data-intensive analytics problem over such logs, rather than as a single-table task. (i) a batch-induced user-item graph that provides collaborative signals without materializing a global graph and remains applicable when item identifiers are missing through reserved unknown-item handling, (ii) business-aware sequence encoders that preserve recency, inter-event gaps, payment context, and goods-table availability, and (iii) cross-view contrastive alignment that transfers user-level intent across businesses while retaining business-specific temporal patterns. To handle zero-inflated and long-tailed cumulative targets, CoGSeq-LTV adopts a zero-inflated mixture log-normal head with MAE-aligned point supervision and validation-calibrated zero-aware inference. Experiments on the BiBiSheng transaction-log dataset show that CoGSeq-LTV improves over representative LTV baselines across businesses and horizons, including under a later out-of-time evaluation window.
core_methodology: Graph-sequence modeling with batch-induced user-item graphs, business-aware sequence encoders, and cross-view contrastive alignment for multi-business transaction analytics
data_sources: Heterogeneous transaction logs from large-scale super-apps with partially available item identifiers and sparse, heavy-tailed value targets
alpha_potential: Potential for understanding user behavior across multiple businesses, but limited direct application to financial markets
